steps.text: 824: Prefect of Hezhou; the 'Inscription on a Humble Room' is traditionally attributed to this time.
steps.text_zh: 824年，任和州刺史，相传在此作《陋室铭》。

steps.text: 826: Meets Bai Juyi at Yangzhou and answers him: 'beside the sunken ship a thousand sails pass by'.
steps.text_zh: 826年，罢和州北归，在扬州初逢白居易，作“沉舟侧畔千帆过”。

steps.text: 831: Prefect of Suzhou, where he organises flood relief.
steps.text_zh: 831年，任苏州刺史，赈济水灾。

steps.text: 842: Dies at Luoyang as a Guest of the Heir Apparent, after years of poetic exchanges with Bai Juyi.
steps.text_zh: 842年，以太子宾客分司东都，与白居易唱和终老，卒于洛阳。

title: Yuan Zhen's life
summary: Bai Juyi's closest friend, Yuan Zhen was exiled for clashing with eunuchs, briefly became chancellor, and ended his career as a governor on the Yangtze.
summary_zh: 元稹与白居易并称“元白”，早年因弹劾权贵、得罪宦官屡遭贬谪，后官至宰相，晚年出镇浙东、武昌，卒于任上。

steps.text: 779: Born in Luoyang; his father dies when he is seven.
steps.text_zh: 779年，生于洛阳，八岁丧父，母亲亲自教读。

steps.text: c. 800: Lodging at Puzhou, he has the youthful romance that, by many accounts, inspired his 'Story of Yingying'.
steps.text_zh: 约800年，寓居蒲州，据说此间经历成为《莺莺传》的原型（一说）。

steps.text: 803: Passes a placement examination with Bai Juyi, beginning a lifelong friendship.
steps.text_zh: 803年，与白居易同登书判拔萃科，授秘书省校书郎，结为终生挚友。

steps.text: 809: As investigating censor in Eastern Sichuan he impeaches the late governor Yan Li for abuses.
steps.text_zh: 809年，以监察御史出使东川，弹奏已故节度使严砺不法。

steps.text: 810: After a brawl with a eunuch at a post station, he is demoted to Jiangling.
steps.text_zh: 810年，在敷水驿与宦官争厅受辱，反被贬江陵府士曹参军。

steps.text: 815: Marshal of Tongzhou; hearing Bai Juyi too has been exiled, he 'sits up in shock from his sickbed'.
steps.text_zh: 815年，贬通州司马，闻白居易贬江州，作“垂死病中惊坐起”。

steps.text: 820: Favoured by Emperor Muzong, he rises fast and becomes chancellor in 822.
steps.text_zh: 820年，得穆宗赏识，迅速升迁，822年拜相。

steps.text: 822: After only months as chancellor, factional infighting sends him out as prefect of Tongzhou.
steps.text_zh: 822年，拜相仅数月即因党争罢为同州刺史。

steps.text: 823: Six years as governor of Eastern Zhejiang at Yuezhou, exchanging poems with Bai Juyi at Hangzhou.
steps.text_zh: 823年，任浙东观察使兼越州刺史六年，与杭州的白居易诗筒往还。

steps.text: 829: Recalled to court as Left Assistant Director of the Department of State.
steps.text_zh: 829年，召回长安任尚书左丞。

steps.text: 830: Appointed military governor of Wuchang.
steps.text_zh: 830年，出任武昌军节度使。

steps.text: 831: Dies suddenly at his post; Bai Juyi writes his epitaph.
steps.text_zh: 831年，暴病卒于任所，白居易为其撰写墓志。

title: Du Mu's travels
summary: Grandson of a chancellor, Du Mu spent his career on provincial staffs and prefectures in the south, writing poems of Yangzhou nights and ancient battlefields.
summary_zh: 杜牧出身名门，多年辗转江南各地幕府和州郡，留下扬州、江南、赤壁等名篇，晚年回到长安樊川。

steps.text: 803: Born into the Du family of Chang'an; his grandfather Du You was chancellor. In 825 he writes the 'Rhapsody on the Epang Palace'.
steps.text_zh: 803年，生于长安杜氏，祖父为宰相杜佑；825年作《阿房宫赋》。

steps.text: 828: Passes the jinshi, with the list posted at the Eastern Capital.
steps.text_zh: 828年，于东都洛阳进士及第。

steps.text: 828: Joins the staff of Shen Chuanshi, governor of Jiangxi.
steps.text_zh: 828年，入江西观察使沈传师幕府。

steps.text: 830: Follows Shen Chuanshi to Xuanzhou.
steps.text_zh: 830年，随沈传师移镇宣州。

steps.text: 833: Secretary to Niu Sengru at Yangzhou; his pleasure-quarter years later become 'ten years' dream of Yangzhou'.
steps.text_zh: 833年，入淮南节度使牛僧孺幕府，流连扬州，后有“十年一觉扬州梦”之句。

steps.text: 835: Investigating censor at the Eastern Capital, narrowly missing the bloody Sweet Dew Incident in Chang'an.
steps.text_zh: 835年，任监察御史分司东都，避开了长安的甘露之变。

steps.text: 842: Prefect of Huangzhou; his quatrain 'Red Cliff' muses on the Three Kingdoms battle.
steps.text_zh: 842年，出任黄州刺史，作《赤壁》“东风不与周郎便”。

steps.text: 844: Prefect of Chizhou, where the poem 'Qingming' is traditionally set (by some accounts).
steps.text_zh: 844年，任池州刺史，相传《清明》“借问酒家何处有”即作于此（一说）。

steps.text: 846: Moved to Muzhou as prefect.
steps.text_zh: 846年，转任睦州刺史。

steps.text: 850: Asks for and receives the prefecture of Huzhou.
steps.text_zh: 850年，自请出任湖州刺史。

steps.text: 852: Back in the capital as a drafting secretary, he burns most of his poems and dies at his Fanchuan villa.
steps.text_zh: 852年，任中书舍人，晚居樊川别墅，临终焚毁大部分诗稿，卒于长安。

title: Li Shangyin's travels
summary: Caught between the Niu and Li factions, Li Shangyin spent his life on provincial staffs from Guilin to Sichuan, writing cryptic, beautiful poems.
summary_zh: 李商隐受牛李党争牵累，一生沉沦幕府，从桂林到东川辗转各地，留下《无题》《锦瑟》等朦胧深婉的诗篇。

steps.text: 813: Born at Huojia, where his father was magistrate (by some accounts); the family home is Huaizhou.
steps.text_zh: 813年，生于获嘉县（一说），祖籍怀州河内。

steps.text: 829: The statesman Linghu Chu takes the young poet onto his staff at Tianping and teaches him parallel prose.
steps.text_zh: 829年，入天平节度使令狐楚幕府任巡官，学习骈文。

steps.text: 837: Passes the jinshi with the help of Linghu Chu's son Linghu Tao.
steps.text_zh: 837年，经令狐綯举荐进士及第。

steps.text: 838: Joins Wang Maoyuan's staff and marries his daughter — seen by the Niu faction as betrayal.
steps.text_zh: 838年，入泾原节度使王茂元幕府并娶其女，被视为背恩，卷入党争。

steps.text: 847: Follows Zheng Ya to Guilin as his secretary.
steps.text_zh: 847年，随郑亚赴桂林，任掌书记。

steps.text: 849: Joins Lu Hongzhi's staff at Xuzhou.
steps.text_zh: 849年，入武宁节度使卢弘止幕府。

steps.text: 851: After his wife's death, serves Liu Zhongying in Eastern Sichuan for some five years; 'Lines Sent North on a Rainy Night' is linked to this time.
steps.text_zh: 851年，妻子病故后入东川节度使柳仲郢幕府约五年，《夜雨寄北》与此时相关。

steps.text: 856: Returns to Chang'an to a minor post in the salt and iron administration.
steps.text_zh: 856年，回到长安，任盐铁推官。

steps.text: 858: Dies in poverty at his home near Zhengzhou.
steps.text_zh: 858年，罢职闲居郑州，病卒。

title: Guo Ziyi's campaigns
summary: The general who saved the Tang: Guo Ziyi led the Shuofang army against An Lushan, retook both capitals, and later turned back Tibetans and Uyghurs.
summary_zh: 郭子仪以朔方军为骨干平定安史之乱，收复两京，又退吐蕃、说回纥，“再造唐室”，以八十五岁高龄善终。

steps.text: 697: Born in Huazhou east of Chang'an.
steps.text_zh: 697年，生于华州郑县。

steps.text: 755: Made military governor of Shuofang as An Lushan rebels; he leads his army east.
steps.text_zh: 755年，安禄山起兵，授朔方节度使，率军东讨。

steps.text: 756: With Li Guangbi crushes Shi Siming's army at Jiashan in Hebei.
steps.text_zh: 756年，与李光弼在嘉山大破史思明。

steps.text: 756: After Tong Pass falls, he brings 50,000 troops to the new Emperor Suzong at Lingwu.
steps.text_zh: 756年，潼关失守后，率五万兵赴灵武拥戴肃宗。

steps.text: 757: With Uyghur help retakes Chang'an, then Luoyang.
steps.text_zh: 757年，借回纥兵收复长安，继而收复洛阳。

steps.text: 759: One of nine generals routed at Yecheng with no supreme commander; he is made a scapegoat.
steps.text_zh: 759年，九节度使围邺城不设元帅，溃败后被夺兵权。

steps.text: 763: When Tibetans seize Chang'an, he rallies scattered troops and drives them out.
steps.text_zh: 763年，吐蕃攻陷长安，他收集散兵，设疑兵逐走吐蕃。

steps.text: 765: Rides unarmed into the Uyghur camp at Jingyang and wins them back to the Tang side.
steps.text_zh: 765年，单骑入回纥营，说服回纥与唐联兵击吐蕃。

steps.text: 768: Moves his headquarters to Binzhou to guard the northwest against Tibet.
steps.text_zh: 768年，移镇邠州，防御吐蕃。

steps.text: 781: Dies in Chang'an aged 85, honoured as Prince of Fenyang.
steps.text_zh: 781年，卒于长安，享年八十五岁，封汾阳郡王。

title: Gao Xianzhi's campaigns
summary: A Goguryeo-born Tang general, Gao Xianzhi crossed the Pamirs to Little Balur, was defeated by the Abbasids at Talas, and was executed after An Lushan's rebels broke through.
summary_zh: 高丽裔唐将高仙芝翻越帕米尔远征小勃律，威震西域；后在怛罗斯败于大食，安史之乱中退守潼关，被冤杀。

steps.text: c. 720: Comes to the Anxi Protectorate with his father, a Goguryeo officer, and becomes a general around twenty.
steps.text_zh: 约720年，随父高舍鸡至安西，约二十岁即授将军。

steps.text: 747: Leads 10,000 men from Anxi through Kashgar towards the Pamirs.
steps.text_zh: 747年，率万人从安西出发，经疏勒向葱岭进军。

steps.place_zh: 小勃律（今巴基斯坦吉尔吉特）
steps.text: 747: Crosses the Pamirs and Darkot Pass and captures Little Balur, cutting Tibet off from the west.
steps.text_zh: 747年，翻越葱岭和坦驹岭，攻破小勃律，切断吐蕃与大食的联系。

steps.text: 748: Made Protector-General of Anxi and military governor of the Four Garrisons.
steps.text_zh: 748年，升任安西四镇节度使。

steps.place_zh: 石国（今乌兹别克斯坦塔什干）
steps.text: 750: Attacks the kingdom of Shi and captures its king, provoking the western states.
steps.text_zh: 750年，攻破石国，俘其国王，引发西域诸国怨恨。

steps.text: 751: Presents his captives at Chang'an and receives high honours.
steps.text_zh: 751年，入朝献俘，加开府仪同三司。

steps.place_zh: 怛罗斯（今哈萨克斯坦塔拉兹）
steps.text: 751: Defeated by the Abbasid army at Talas when his Karluk allies defect.
steps.text_zh: 751年，与大食军战于怛罗斯，葛逻禄部倒戈，唐军大败。

steps.text: 755: Sent east against An Lushan; after Luoyang falls he pulls back from Shaanzhou to defend Tong Pass.
steps.text_zh: 755年，任副元帅东讨安禄山，洛阳失陷后从陕州退守潼关。

steps.text: 756: Slandered by the eunuch Bian Lingcheng, he is executed at Tong Pass with Feng Changqing (early 756 by the Western calendar).
steps.text_zh: 756年，遭监军宦官边令诚诬告，与封常清同被斩于潼关军中。

title: Huang Chao's campaigns
summary: A failed examination candidate and salt smuggler, Huang Chao led a rebellion across nearly all of China, sacked Guangzhou, took Chang'an, and died in the Shandong hills.
summary_zh: 落第书生、私盐贩子黄巢起兵后转战大半个中国，攻陷广州，入长安建大齐，最终败死山东狼虎谷，唐朝自此名存实亡。

steps.text: 835: Born into a family of salt smugglers at Yuanju (birth year uncertain).
steps.text_zh: 835年，生于曹州冤句贩盐之家（生年不详）。

steps.text: c. 865: Fails the jinshi in Chang'an; tradition credits him with the defiant poem 'The Chrysanthemum' — 'the city will be filled with golden armour'.
steps.text_zh: 约865年，入京应进士举落第，相传作《不第后赋菊》“满城尽带黄金甲”。

steps.text: 875: Raises troops with his kinsmen to join Wang Xianzhi's rebellion.
steps.text_zh: 875年，与子侄起兵响应王仙芝。

steps.place_zh: 仙霞岭（今浙江江山与福建浦城间）
steps.text: 878: After Wang Xianzhi's death he leads the rebels south, cutting a 700-li road over the mountains into Fujian.
steps.text_zh: 878年，王仙芝死后，率众南下，开仙霞岭山路七百里入闽。

steps.text: 879: Captures and sacks Guangzhou, killing many foreign merchants.
steps.text_zh: 879年，攻陷广州，大肆屠杀，据载外商死者甚众。

steps.text: 880: Having marched north, his army crosses the Yangtze at Caishi.
steps.text_zh: 880年，北上转战，从采石渡过长江。

steps.text: 880: Takes the Eastern Capital without a fight.
steps.text_zh: 880年，兵不血刃攻占东都洛阳。

steps.text: 880: Enters Chang'an as Emperor Xizong flees; proclaims himself emperor of Great Qi.
steps.text_zh: 880年，攻入长安，僖宗逃往蜀中，次年称帝，国号大齐。

steps.text: 884: Driven from Chang'an (883), he besieges Chenzhou for some 300 days in vain.
steps.text_zh: 884年，883年退出长安后围攻陈州近三百日不下。

steps.text: 884: Defeated by Li Keyong and deserted by his followers, he dies at Langhu Valley.
steps.text_zh: 884年，被李克用击败，众叛亲离，死于泰山狼虎谷。

title: Lu Yu's travels
summary: A foundling raised in a temple, Lu Yu travelled the tea lands of the Yangtze and wrote the world's first book on tea at Huzhou.
summary_zh: 陆羽是寺院收养的弃婴，一生遍访长江南北茶区，在湖州写成世界第一部茶学专著《茶经》，被尊为“茶圣”。

steps.text: 733: A foundling taken in by the monk Zhiji at the Longgai Temple, Jingling.
steps.text_zh: 733年，被竟陵龙盖寺智积禅师收养。

steps.text: c. 754: Leaves home to tour the tea mountains of the Three Gorges and Ba-Shu borders.
steps.text_zh: 约754年，出游巴山峡川，考察茶事。

steps.text: c. 758: Fleeing the An Lushan war south of the Yangtze, he tastes and ranks the springs of Huishan at Wuxi.
steps.text_zh: 约758年，因安史之乱过江南下，品评无锡惠山泉。

steps.text: 760: Settles by the Tiao river at Huzhou, befriends the monk Jiaoran and writes 'The Classic of Tea'.
steps.text_zh: 760年，隐居湖州苕溪，与诗僧皎然结为忘年交，著《茶经》。

steps.text: 773: Helps prefect Yan Zhenqing compile his rhyme dictionary; Yan builds the Three Gui Pavilion in his honour.
steps.text_zh: 773年，协助刺史颜真卿编纂《韵海镜源》，颜为其建“三癸亭”。

steps.text: c. 785: Lives for a time at Shangrao, where 'Lu Yu Spring' still bears his name.
steps.text_zh: 约785年，移居信州上饶，今存“陆羽泉”。

steps.text: c. 788: Stays at Hongzhou.
steps.text_zh: 约788年，客居洪州玉芝观。

steps.text: c. 789: Joins the staff of Li Fu, governor of Lingnan, at Guangzhou.
steps.text_zh: 约789年，应岭南节度使李复之邀入幕广州。

steps.text: c. 793: Lives at Tiger Hill in Suzhou, digging a well for tea.
steps.text_zh: 约793年，寓居苏州虎丘，凿井煮茶。

steps.text: 804: Dies at Huzhou and is buried on Mount Zhu.
steps.text_zh: 804年，卒于湖州，葬杼山。

title: Zhao Kuangyin's campaigns
summary: A Later Zhou general who seized the throne at Chenqiao, Zhao Kuangyin founded the Song, crushed rival generals, took their armies with a cup of wine, and died mysteriously in 976.
summary_zh: 后周大将赵匡胤陈桥兵变黄袍加身，建立宋朝；平定李筠、李重进，杯酒释兵权，先南后北统一大半个中国，976年在“烛影斧声”中猝死。

steps.place_zh: 洛阳夹马营（今河南洛阳）
steps.text: 927: Born at the Jiama barracks in Luoyang, son of a palace-guard officer.
steps.text_zh: 927年，生于洛阳夹马营，父亲为禁军军官。

steps.text: 949: After years of wandering, joins Guo Wei's army besieging rebel Hezhong.
steps.text_zh: 949年，游历多年后，投奔正在讨伐河中叛乱的郭威。

steps.text: 954: Turns the tide at Gaoping when the Later Zhou line wavers; Emperor Shizong promotes him.
steps.text_zh: 954年，高平之战中奋勇冲阵扭转战局，受周世宗重用。

steps.text: 956: In the Huainan campaign, storms Qingliu Pass and takes Chuzhou from the Southern Tang.
steps.text_zh: 956年，征淮南时奇袭清流关，攻克滁州。

steps.text: 959: Commands on Shizong's northern campaign that retakes the passes from the Liao.
steps.text_zh: 959年，随周世宗北伐，收复瓦桥关等关南之地。

steps.text: 960: His troops drape a yellow robe over him at Chenqiao; he returns to Kaifeng as emperor of Song.
steps.text_zh: 960年，陈桥兵变，黄袍加身，回师开封建立宋朝。

steps.text: 960: Personally crushes the revolt of Li Yun at Zezhou.
steps.text_zh: 960年，亲征平定昭义节度使李筠叛乱。

steps.text: 960: Marches on Yangzhou and ends Li Chongjin's revolt.
steps.text_zh: 960年，亲征扬州，平定李重进叛乱。

steps.text: 961: Persuades his top generals over wine to give up their commands.
steps.text_zh: 961年，“杯酒释兵权”，解除禁军宿将兵权。

steps.text: 969: Personally besieges Taiyuan, capital of the Northern Han, but must withdraw.
steps.text_zh: 969年，亲征北汉围攻太原，久攻不下而还。

steps.text: 976: Dies suddenly after a night drinking with his brother, who succeeds him.
steps.text_zh: 976年，与弟赵光义夜饮后猝死，留下“烛影斧声”之谜。

title: Ouyang Xiu's life
summary: Ouyang Xiu led the Song prose revival, served the Qingli reforms, wrote at Chuzhou as the 'Old Drunkard', and retired to his beloved Yingzhou.
summary_zh: 欧阳修一生三遭贬谪，支持庆历新政，在滁州自号“醉翁”，主持科举提携苏轼兄弟，晚年退居颍州。

steps.text: 1007: Born at Mianzhou where his father was a judicial officer.
steps.text_zh: 1007年，生于绵州，父亲任推官。

steps.text: 1010: His father dies; his mother raises him at Suizhou, teaching him to write with a reed in the sand.
steps.text_zh: 1010年，父亲去世，随母投奔随州叔父，母亲“画荻教子”。

steps.text: 1031: After passing the jinshi (1030), serves at the Western Capital with Mei Yaochen and Yin Zhu.
steps.text_zh: 1031年，进士及第后任西京留守推官，与梅尧臣、尹洙等交游。

steps.text: 1036: Demoted to magistrate of Yiling for defending Fan Zhongyan.
steps.text_zh: 1036年，因声援范仲淹被贬夷陵县令。

steps.text: 1043: As remonstrance official he champions Fan Zhongyan's Qingli reforms.
steps.text_zh: 1043年，任谏官，积极支持范仲淹庆历新政。

steps.text: 1045: Demoted to Chuzhou after the reforms fail; there he writes 'The Old Drunkard's Pavilion'.
steps.text_zh: 1045年，新政失败后贬知滁州，作《醉翁亭记》。

steps.text: 1048: Prefect of Yangzhou; builds the Pingshan Hall.
steps.text_zh: 1048年，知扬州，建平山堂。

steps.text: 1049: Prefect of Yingzhou, which he comes to love and chooses for his retirement.
steps.text_zh: 1049年，知颍州，爱其西湖风物，决意终老于此。

steps.text: 1057: Chief examiner; passes Su Shi, Su Zhe and Zeng Gong. He also leads the 'New Book of Tang' (1060).
steps.text_zh: 1057年，主持礼部贡举，录取苏轼、苏辙、曾巩，后主修《新唐书》。

steps.text: 1068: Prefect of Qingzhou; he halts the Green Sprouts loans of Wang Anshi's new laws there.
steps.text_zh: 1068年，知青州，反对并擅停青苗法。

steps.text: 1072: Retired as the 'Retired Scholar of Six Ones' (1071), he dies at Yingzhou.
steps.text_zh: 1072年，自号“六一居士”致仕（1071年），卒于颍州。

title: Sima Guang's life
summary: Statesman and historian, Sima Guang opposed Wang Anshi's reforms, spent fifteen years in Luoyang writing the 'Comprehensive Mirror', and returned as chancellor to undo the new laws.
summary_zh: 司马光反对王安石变法，退居洛阳十五年编成《资治通鉴》；神宗死后入朝为相，尽废新法，数月后病逝。

steps.text: 1019: Born at Guangshan where his father was magistrate; legend tells of him smashing a water jar to save a drowning friend.
steps.text_zh: 1019年，生于光山县（父任县令），留有“砸缸救友”的传说。

steps.text: 1038: Passes the jinshi in the top group at age 19.
steps.text_zh: 1038年，十九岁进士甲科及第。

steps.text: 1055: Serves his patron Pang Ji as vice-prefect of Bingzhou on the northern frontier.
steps.text_zh: 1055年，随恩师庞籍任并州通判。

steps.text: 1061: As remonstrance official urges Emperor Renzong to name an heir; in 1066 begins his chronicle of history.
steps.text_zh: 1061年，任知谏院，力请仁宗立储；1066年奉诏编修通史。

steps.text: 1070: Having fought Wang Anshi's new laws in court, he takes a post at Yongxing.
steps.text_zh: 1070年，反对王安石变法未果，出知永兴军。

steps.text: 1071: Retires to Luoyang, builds the Garden of Solitary Pleasure and works on his history.
steps.text_zh: 1071年，退居洛阳，筑“独乐园”，专心修史。

steps.text: 1084: Presents the 294-chapter 'Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government' after 19 years' work.
steps.text_zh: 1084年，历时十九年编成《资治通鉴》二百九十四卷，进呈神宗。

steps.text: 1086: Recalled as chancellor (1085), he repeals the new laws, then dies in office.
steps.text_zh: 1086年，1085年还朝，拜相后尽废新法，数月后病逝于开封。

title: Shen Kuo's travels
summary: The polymath Shen Kuo served as county official, court astronomer, envoy to the Liao and frontier commander against Xixia before retiring to his Dream Brook garden in Runzhou.
summary_zh: 博学家沈括历任县吏、司天监、使辽使臣和西北边帅，永乐城之败后被贬，晚年退居润州梦溪园著书。

steps.text: 1031: Born in Qiantang into an official family; as a boy he follows his father to postings around the empire.
steps.text_zh: 1031年，生于钱塘官宦之家，少年时随父宦游各地。

steps.text: c. 1054: As registrar of Shuyang county he drains marshland and builds dikes, turning it into farmland.
steps.text_zh: 约1054年，任海州沭阳县主簿，主持疏浚沟渠、筑堤造田。

steps.text: 1063: Passes the jinshi exam and soon joins the imperial library, later heading the Bureau of Astronomy.
steps.text_zh: 1063年，进士及第，入京任职馆阁，后提举司天监。

steps.text: 1075: Sent as envoy to the Liao emperor's camp, he uses archival maps to argue down Liao claims on the Hedong border.
steps.text_zh: 1075年，出使辽国，凭档案据理力争河东地界，挫辽方之索。

steps.text: 1080: Made military commissioner at Yanzhou on the Xixia frontier, where he notes the 'stone oil' (petroleum) of the region.
steps.text_zh: 1080年，知延州、任鄜延路经略安抚使，在当地记下“石油”之名。

steps.text: 1082: The new fortress of Yongle falls to Xixia with huge losses; Shen Kuo is blamed and demoted.
steps.text_zh: 1082年，新筑永乐城被西夏攻陷，宋军死伤惨重，沈括坐罪贬官。

steps.text: 1083: Placed under supervision in Suizhou as a disgraced official.
steps.text_zh: 1083年，以团练副使安置随州。

steps.text: c. 1085: Moved to Xiuzhou, where he completes his great atlas of the empire, the Shouling Tu.
steps.text_zh: 约1085年，移秀州，完成全国地图《守令图》。

steps.text: 1088: Settles at his Dream Brook garden in Runzhou and writes the Dream Pool Essays.
steps.text_zh: 1088年，定居润州梦溪园，撰写《梦溪笔谈》。

steps.text: 1095: Dies at Dream Brook garden.
steps.text_zh: 1095年，卒于梦溪园。

title: Huang Tingjian's travels
summary: Poet and calligrapher Huang Tingjian rose through county posts to the Song court, then, as a member of Su Shi's circle, spent his last decade in exile in Sichuan and Guangxi.
summary_zh: 诗人、书法家黄庭坚由地方小官入朝修史，因属苏轼一派，晚年屡遭贬谪，辗转黔州、戎州，客死宜州。

steps.text: 1045: Born in Fenning, Hongzhou, into a literary family.
steps.text_zh: 1045年，生于洪州分宁书香之家。

steps.text: 1068: After passing the jinshi exam he takes his first post as sheriff of Ye county.
steps.text_zh: 1068年，进士及第后出任叶县尉。

steps.text: 1072: Teaches at the Imperial Academy branch in Daming; begins corresponding with Su Shi.
steps.text_zh: 1072年，任北京国子监教授，开始与苏轼书信往来。

steps.text: 1080: Magistrate of Taihe county, Jizhou.
steps.text_zh: 1080年，知吉州太和县。

steps.text: 1086: Called to the capital to edit the Veritable Records of Shenzong; with Su Shi at the centre of the Yuanyou literary circle.
steps.text_zh: 1086年，召入京任校书郎、修《神宗实录》，与苏轼等诗酒唱和。

steps.text: 1095: Accused of distorting the Records, he is exiled to Qianzhou in the far southwest.
steps.text_zh: 1095年，以修实录“不实”获罪，贬涪州别驾、黔州安置。

steps.text: 1098: Moved further up the Yangtze to Rongzhou, where his calligraphy matures.
steps.text_zh: 1098年，移戎州安置，书艺日臻化境。

steps.text: 1101: Pardoned under Huizong, he waits at Jingzhou for a new post.
steps.text_zh: 1101年，徽宗即位遇赦，东归途中寓居荆州。

steps.text: 1102: Governor of Taiping prefecture for just nine days before being dismissed.
steps.text_zh: 1102年，知太平州，仅九日即罢。

steps.text: 1105: Exiled again in 1104 to remote Yizhou, he dies there the next year.
steps.text_zh: 1105年，前一年再贬宜州，次年卒于贬所。

title: Su Zhe's travels
summary: Su Shi's younger brother Su Zhe left Sichuan for the capital, served in provincial posts during the reform years, reached high office under Yuanyou, and after exile to the far south retired to Yingchang.
summary_zh: 苏轼之弟苏辙出蜀入京，变法年间辗转地方，元祐时官至门下侍郎，晚年远贬雷州、循州，终老颍昌。

steps.text: 1039: Born in Meishan, younger brother of Su Shi.
steps.text_zh: 1039年，生于眉州眉山，为苏轼之弟。

steps.text: 1057: Having travelled to the capital with father and brother, passes the jinshi exam alongside Su Shi.
steps.text_zh: 1057年，随父兄入京，与苏轼同榜进士及第。

steps.text: 1070: After opposing Wang Anshi's reforms he leaves the capital to teach in Chenzhou.
steps.text_zh: 1070年，因反对王安石新法，出为陈州教授。

steps.text: 1074: Secretary in Qizhou.
steps.text_zh: 1074年，任齐州掌书记。

steps.text: 1077: Assistant administrator at the Southern Capital, Yingtian.
steps.text_zh: 1077年，任南京签书判官。

steps.text: 1080: Punished for pleading for his brother in the Crow Terrace case, he is demoted to supervise the salt and wine tax in Yunzhou.
steps.text_zh: 1080年，因上书营救乌台诗案中的兄长，贬监筠州盐酒税。

steps.text: 1086: Recalled under the Yuanyou regency; rises to vice-director of the Chancellery by 1091.
steps.text_zh: 1086年，元祐更化，召回朝廷，1091年官至门下侍郎。

steps.text: 1097: After the reformists return to power he is exiled to Leizhou; his brother Su Shi crosses to Hainan nearby.
steps.text_zh: 1097年，新党复起，贬雷州安置，与渡海赴儋州的苏轼隔海相望。

steps.text: 1098: Moved to Xunzhou in the hills of eastern Guangdong.
steps.text_zh: 1098年，移循州安置。

steps.text: 1112: Pardoned in 1100, he settled in Yingchang as the 'Old Man of the Ying Riverside' and dies there.
steps.text_zh: 1112年，自1100年遇赦后退居颍昌，自号颍滨遗老，卒于此。

title: Mi Fu's travels
summary: The eccentric calligrapher Mi Fu held minor posts across the south, met Su Shi in exile, made Runzhou his home and ended as Huizong's Erudite of Calligraphy and Painting.
summary_zh: 书画家米芾一生多任地方小官，曾赴黄州拜访苏轼，定居润州，晚年任书画学博士，卒于淮阳军任上。

steps.text: 1051: Born to a family of Taiyuan origin settled in Xiangyang, hence his name 'the Xiangyang eccentric'.
steps.text_zh: 1051年，生于襄阳（祖籍太原），后自号“襄阳漫士”。

steps.text: c. 1071: Thanks to his mother's service to the empress, he receives a post as sheriff of Hanguang in Guangdong.
steps.text_zh: 约1071年，因母亲侍奉宣仁皇后，得补浛洸尉。

steps.text: c. 1078: Serves as a clerk in Changsha.
steps.text_zh: 约1078年，任长沙掾。

steps.text: 1082: Visits the exiled Su Shi, who urges him to study Jin-dynasty calligraphy.
steps.text_zh: 1082年，赴黄州拜访贬居的苏轼，苏轼劝其学晋人书法。

steps.text: 1088: Writes the Shu Silk Scroll and the Tiaoxi Poems scroll, masterpieces of his running script.
steps.text_zh: 1088年，在湖州书《蜀素帖》《苕溪诗卷》。

steps.text: c. 1090: Makes Runzhou his home, later building his Haiyue studio there.
steps.text_zh: 约1090年，定居润州，后筑海岳庵。

steps.text: 1094: Magistrate of Yongqiu county.
steps.text_zh: 1094年，知雍丘县。

steps.text: 1104: Appointed Erudite of Calligraphy and Painting at Huizong's court.
steps.text_zh: 1104年，任书画学博士，为徽宗所赏识。

steps.text: 1107: Dies in office as governor of Huaiyang; he is buried in Dantu near Runzhou.
steps.text_zh: 1107年，卒于知淮阳军任上，葬于润州丹徒。

title: Kou Zhun's life
summary: The outspoken minister Kou Zhun steadied Emperor Zhenzong at Chanyuan in 1004, but court rivals sent him repeatedly into provincial exile, ending in Leizhou at the tip of the mainland.
summary_zh: 直臣寇准澶渊之役力劝真宗亲征，促成和议，却屡遭排挤，几度外放，最终远贬雷州而卒。

steps.text: 961: Born in Xiagui, Huazhou.
steps.text_zh: 961年，生于华州下邽。

steps.text: 980: Passes the jinshi exam at nineteen and is sent to govern Badong in the Three Gorges.
steps.text_zh: 980年，十九岁中进士，出任巴东知县。

steps.text: c. 995: Trusted by Emperor Taizong, he urges him to name his heir; becomes assistant chief minister.
steps.text_zh: 约995年，深得太宗信任，力劝早立太子，拜参知政事。

steps.text: 996: Demoted to govern Dengzhou after clashing with colleagues.
steps.text_zh: 996年，因与同僚争执，罢知邓州。

steps.text: 1004: As chief minister he persuades Zhenzong to lead troops to Chanzhou against the Liao, leading to the Chanyuan treaty.
steps.text_zh: 1004年，任宰相，力排众议，劝真宗亲征澶州，促成澶渊之盟。

steps.text: 1006: Slandered by Wang Qinruo, he loses the chancellorship and governs Shanzhou.
steps.text_zh: 1006年，遭王钦若谗毁罢相，出知陕州。

steps.text: c. 1017: Governor of Yongxing (Chang'an).
steps.text_zh: 约1017年，判永兴军。

steps.text: 1019: Recalled as chief minister once more.
steps.text_zh: 1019年，再度入朝拜相。

steps.text: 1020: Ousted by Ding Wei and exiled to Daozhou.
steps.text_zh: 1020年，为丁谓所排，贬道州司马。

steps.text: 1023: Exiled further to Leizhou in 1022, he dies there.
steps.text_zh: 1023年，前一年再贬雷州司户参军，卒于贬所。

title: Di Qing's campaigns
summary: A tattooed common soldier, Di Qing made his name on the Xixia frontier, crushed Nong Zhigao's rising with a night march over Kunlun Pass, and rose to head the Bureau of Military Affairs.
summary_zh: 狄青出身行伍、面有刺字，在西北抗击西夏成名，夜袭昆仑关平定侬智高，官至枢密使，后遭猜忌外放陈州而卒。

steps.text: 1008: Born to a poor family in Xihe, Fenzhou.
steps.text_zh: 1008年，生于汾州西河贫寒之家。

steps.text: c. 1024: Taking the blame for his brother, he is tattooed and enrolled as a soldier in the capital guards.
steps.text_zh: 约1024年，代兄受过，黥面从军，入京为禁军骑卒。

steps.text: 1038: Sent to the frontier when Xixia declares independence; he fights in a bronze mask with loose hair.
steps.text_zh: 1038年，西夏建国，调赴保安军前线，披发戴铜面具冲锋陷阵。

steps.text: 1040: Fan Zhongyan, commanding at Yanzhou, gives him the Zuo Commentary and urges him to study the classics of war.
steps.text_zh: 1040年，范仲淹镇守延州，授以《左氏春秋》，勉其读书。

steps.text: 1052: Now Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs, he volunteers to lead the campaign against Nong Zhigao.
steps.text_zh: 1052年，已任枢密副使，上表请缨南征侬智高。

steps.text: 1053: During the Lantern Festival he slips his army over Kunlun Pass at night and routs Nong Zhigao.
steps.text_zh: 1053年，上元夜乘夜越过昆仑关，大破侬智高。

steps.text: 1053: Retakes Yongzhou; Nong Zhigao flees to Dali.
steps.text_zh: 1053年，收复邕州，侬智高逃往大理。

steps.text: 1053: Returns in triumph and becomes Commissioner of Military Affairs, rare for a soldier.
steps.text_zh: 1053年，凯旋回京，拜枢密使，以武人居此职极为罕见。

steps.text: 1057: Distrusted by civil officials, he was sent to govern Chenzhou in 1056 and dies there.
steps.text_zh: 1057年，因文臣猜忌，前一年出知陈州，次年病卒。

title: Bao Zheng's life
summary: Bao Zheng, the incorruptible 'Judge Bao', served as magistrate, censor and prefect of Kaifeng, earning a reputation for justice that turned him into a folk hero.
summary_zh: 包拯历任知县、知州、御史，权知开封府时铁面无私，身后被尊为“包青天”。

steps.text: 999: Born in Hefei, Luzhou.
steps.text_zh: 999年，生于庐州合肥。

steps.text: 1037: After years caring for his parents, he takes his first post as magistrate of Tianchang, famed for solving the 'ox-tongue' case.
steps.text_zh: 1037年，奉养双亲多年后出任天长知县，以“割牛舌案”闻名。

steps.text: 1040: Governor of Duanzhou, home of the famous inkstones; he leaves without taking a single one.
steps.text_zh: 1040年，知端州，岁满离任不持一砚归。

steps.text: 1043: Becomes an investigating censor in the capital, known for blunt memorials.
steps.text_zh: 1043年，入京任监察御史，直言敢谏。

steps.text: c. 1052: Governor of Yingzhou on the Liao frontier.
steps.text_zh: 约1052年，出知瀛州。

steps.text: c. 1054: Governs his home prefecture of Luzhou, where he flogs his own uncle for breaking the law.
steps.text_zh: 约1054年，知庐州，亲舅犯法亦依律杖责。

steps.text: 1056: Acting prefect of Kaifeng; his incorruptibility gives rise to the saying 'Bribery doesn't reach Old Bao'.
steps.text_zh: 1056年，权知开封府，京师有“关节不到，有阎罗包老”之语。

steps.text: 1062: Dies in office as Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs; he is buried in Hefei.
steps.text_zh: 1062年，卒于枢密副使任上，归葬合肥。

title: Xin Qiji's travels
summary: Born under Jin rule in Shandong, Xin Qiji led a daring raid south to join the Song, served as a capable governor across the south, and spent long years in forced retirement writing ci poems about the lost north.
summary_zh: 辛弃疾生于金占山东，率众南归，历任江南各地帅守，却屡遭弹劾闲居上饶、铅山，以豪放词抒写恢复之志。

steps.text: 1140: Born in Licheng under Jin rule; his grandfather raises him to hope for the Song's return.
steps.text_zh: 1140年，生于金国治下的济南历城，祖父常勉其不忘故国。

steps.text: 1161: As Jin invades the Song, he raises some two thousand men and joins Geng Jing's rebel army.
steps.text_zh: 1161年，金主完颜亮南侵，聚众二千人投奔耿京义军。

steps.text: 1162: Sent south to meet Emperor Gaozong at Jiankang; on his way back, hearing Geng Jing was murdered, he storms the traitor's camp with fifty riders and brings him south.
steps.text_zh: 1162年，奉表南下建康见高宗；归途闻耿京被害，率五十骑闯入金营擒叛徒张安国南归。

steps.text: 1172: Governor of war-ravaged Chuzhou, he restores its markets and settlers.
steps.text_zh: 1172年，知滁州，招抚流散，恢复市井。

steps.text: 1180: As pacification commissioner of Hunan he founds the elite Flying Tiger Army.
steps.text_zh: 1180年，任湖南安抚使，创建飞虎军。

steps.text: 1181: Impeached, he retires to his new Daihu estate at Shangrao for a decade of poetry.
steps.text_zh: 1181年，遭弹劾落职，退居上饶带湖新居近十年。

steps.text: 1192: Recalled as judicial and then pacification commissioner of Fujian.
steps.text_zh: 1192年，起任福建提点刑狱，后任福建安抚使。

steps.text: 1196: Dismissed again, he moves to Piaoquan at Qishan in Yanshan.
steps.text_zh: 1196年，再遭罢黜，移居铅山期思瓢泉。

steps.text: 1203: Recalled during Han Tuozhou's war preparations as governor of Shaoxing.
steps.text_zh: 1203年，韩侂胄谋北伐，起知绍兴府兼浙东安抚使。

steps.text: 1205: Governor of Zhenjiang, he writes 'Recalling the Past at Beigu Pavilion', warning against a rash war.
steps.text_zh: 1205年，知镇江府，作《永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古》，告诫勿轻启战端。

steps.text: 1207: Dies at home in Yanshan, reportedly crying 'Kill the enemy!'
steps.text_zh: 1207年，病逝于铅山，相传临终大呼“杀贼”。

title: Yang Wanli's travels
summary: Yang Wanli, one of the four great poets of the Southern Song, served in provincial and court posts from Guangdong to Jiangnan before retiring to his home in Jishui for his last fourteen years.
summary_zh: 南宋“中兴四大诗人”之一杨万里宦游岭南、江南与临安，晚年退居吉水故里十四年，以“诚斋体”名世。

steps.text: 1127: Born in Jishui, Jizhou, the year the Northern Song fell.
steps.text_zh: 1127年，生于吉州吉水，正值北宋灭亡。

steps.text: c. 1155: After the jinshi exam of 1154, his first post is as a clerk in Ganzhou.
steps.text_zh: 约1155年，1154年中进士后，初任赣州司户参军。

steps.text: c. 1159: Assistant magistrate of Lingling, where the exiled general Zhang Jun teaches him 'sincerity', the source of his studio name Chengzhai.
steps.text_zh: 约1159年，任零陵县丞，受谪居于此的张浚“正心诚意”之教，遂名书斋为“诚斋”。

steps.text: c. 1170: Serves at court in Lin'an as an erudite of the Imperial Academy.
steps.text_zh: 约1170年，在临安任国子博士等职。

steps.text: 1178: Governor of Changzhou; he abandons imitating older poets and finds his own fresh, colloquial voice.
steps.text_zh: 1178年，任常州知州，诗风大变，自成清新活泼的“诚斋体”。

steps.text: 1180: Commissioner of tea, salt and granaries in Guangdong; helps suppress a local uprising.
steps.text_zh: 1180年，任广东提举常平茶盐，参与平定地方叛乱。

steps.text: 1186: Back at court as a senior official; in 1189 he escorts Jin envoys along the Huai.
steps.text_zh: 1186年，入朝任吏部员外郎等职，1189年曾奉命接伴金使至淮河。

steps.text: 1190: Transport commissioner of Jiangdong; he resigns in 1192 after opposing a plan to issue iron coins.
steps.text_zh: 1190年，任江东转运副使，1192年因反对推行铁钱辞官。

steps.text: 1206: Retired in Jishui since 1192, he dies there, reportedly in grief at Han Tuozhou's reckless war.
steps.text_zh: 1206年，自1192年起退居吉水，闻韩侂胄轻启战端，忧愤而卒。

title: Fan Chengda's travels
summary: Fan Chengda braved a mission to the Jin capital, governed from Guilin to Chengdu, recorded his journeys in celebrated travel diaries, and retired to Stone Lake outside Suzhou.
summary_zh: 范成大出使金国不辱使命，宦游桂林、成都、明州、建康，留下多部游记，晚年退居苏州石湖。

steps.text: 1126: Born in Wu county, Suzhou.
steps.text_zh: 1126年，生于平江府吴县。

steps.text: c. 1156: After passing the jinshi exam in 1154, his first post is as a clerk in Huizhou.
steps.text_zh: 约1156年，1154年中进士后，初任徽州司户参军。

steps.text: 1167: Governor of Chuzhou, he restores the ancient Tongji weir.
steps.text_zh: 1167年，知处州，修复通济堰。

steps.text: 1170: As envoy to the Jin he presses for the return of the Song imperial tombs and nearly loses his life; his diary Lanpei Lu records the ruined north.
steps.text_zh: 1170年，出使金国，不畏强权力争陵寝之地，几遭不测，作《揽辔录》及七十二首使金绝句。

steps.text: 1173: Governor of Guilin; his notes become the Guihai Yuheng Zhi on the south's landscapes and peoples.
steps.text_zh: 1173年，知静江府，后撰《桂海虞衡志》记岭南风物。

steps.text: 1175: Military commissioner of Sichuan, with the poet Lu You on his staff.
steps.text_zh: 1175年，任四川制置使，陆游入其幕府。

steps.text: 1178: Having sailed down the Yangtze in 1177 (recorded in his Wuchuan Lu), he briefly becomes assistant chief minister.
steps.text_zh: 1178年，前一年顺江东下（著《吴船录》），回朝一度拜参知政事。

steps.text: c. 1179: Governor of Mingzhou and coastal commander.
steps.text_zh: 约1179年，知明州兼沿海制置使。

steps.text: c. 1181: Governor of Jiankang, where he organises famine relief.
steps.text_zh: 约1181年，知建康府，赈济灾民。

steps.text: 1193: Retired at Stone Lake, where he wrote the Sixty Seasonal Rural Poems, he dies there.
steps.text_zh: 1193年，晚年退居石湖，曾作《四时田园杂兴》六十首，卒于家。

title: Zhu Xi's travels
summary: Neo-Confucian master Zhu Xi spent most of his life teaching in the hills of northern Fujian, with short but influential official postings that revived academies and spread his Four Books.
summary_zh: 理学大师朱熹一生大半在闽北讲学著述，几次短暂出仕，兴复书院、推行社仓、刊刻《四书》，影响后世七百年。

steps.text: 1130: Born in Youxi, where his father is a local official.
steps.text_zh: 1130年，生于南剑州尤溪，父朱松时任尤溪县尉。

steps.place_zh: 崇安五夫里（福建武夷山）
steps.text: 1143: After his father's death he settles with his mother at Wufu in Chong'an.
steps.text_zh: 1143年，父亲去世，随母迁居崇安五夫里。

steps.text: 1148: Passes the jinshi exam at eighteen.
steps.text_zh: 1148年，十八岁中进士。

steps.text: 1153: Registrar of Tong'an county, his first post.
steps.text_zh: 1153年，任泉州同安县主簿。

steps.text: 1160: Formally becomes a disciple of Li Tong at Yanping.
steps.text_zh: 1160年，赴延平正式拜李侗为师。

steps.place_zh: 崇安五夫里（福建武夷山）
steps.text: 1171: Founds a community granary at Wufu to lend grain in famine years.
steps.text_zh: 1171年，在五夫里创立社仓，荒年低息借贷粮食。

steps.text: 1175: Debates the Lu brothers on how to pursue learning at the Goose Lake meeting.
steps.text_zh: 1175年，与陆九渊兄弟会于鹅湖寺，辩论为学之方。

steps.text: 1179: As governor of Nankang he rebuilds the White Deer Grotto Academy.
steps.text_zh: 1179年，知南康军，重建白鹿洞书院。

steps.text: 1190: Governor of Zhangzhou, where he prints his Collected Commentaries on the Four Books.
steps.text_zh: 1190年，知漳州，刊刻《四书章句集注》。

steps.text: 1194: Governor of Tanzhou, he revives the Yuelu Academy; later that year he lectures the new emperor for just 46 days.
steps.text_zh: 1194年，知潭州，修复岳麓书院；同年入朝为宁宗侍讲仅四十六日。

steps.text: 1200: Branded 'false learning' in the Qingyuan ban, he dies at his Kaoting academy.
steps.text_zh: 1200年，庆元党禁中被斥为“伪学”，卒于建阳考亭。

title: Emperor Gaozong's flight and reign
summary: The only prince to escape the Jin capture of Kaifeng, Zhao Gou was crowned at Yingtian and fled south across the Yangtze and out to sea before founding the Southern Song at Lin'an.
summary_zh: 赵构在靖康之变中幸免于难，于应天府即位，一路南逃渡江、入海，最终定都临安，开创南宋。

steps.text: 1107: Born in Kaifeng, ninth son of Emperor Huizong.
steps.text_zh: 1107年，生于开封，为宋徽宗第九子。

steps.text: 1126: Sent as envoy to the Jin, he is turned back by Zong Ze at Cizhou and made Grand Marshal of the armies in Hebei at Xiangzhou.
steps.text_zh: 1126年，奉命出使金营，在磁州被宗泽劝止，于相州开大元帅府。

steps.text: 1127: With his father and brother taken north, he ascends the throne at Yingtian.
steps.text_zh: 1127年，徽钦二帝被掳，在南京应天府即位。

steps.text: 1128: Moves the court to Yangzhou; in early 1129 a Jin raid sends him fleeing across the Yangtze.
steps.text_zh: 1128年，驻跸扬州；次年初金兵奔袭，仓皇渡江南逃。

steps.text: 1129: Briefly forced to abdicate by the Miao-Liu mutiny in Hangzhou, then restored.
steps.text_zh: 1129年，在杭州遭苗刘兵变逼迫退位，旋即复辟。

steps.text: 1130: Pursued by the Jin, he takes to the sea from Mingzhou and drifts along the coast to Wenzhou.
steps.text_zh: 1130年，金兵“搜山检海”，自明州乘船入海，漂泊至温州。

steps.text: 1131: Settles in Yuezhou, which he renames Shaoxing.
steps.text_zh: 1131年，驻跸越州，改名绍兴府。

steps.text: 1137: Moves forward to Jiankang as Yue Fei and others campaign north.
steps.text_zh: 1137年，移驻建康，前线岳飞等将北伐。

steps.text: 1138: Makes Lin'an the capital; in 1141 he makes peace with the Jin and has Yue Fei put to death.
steps.text_zh: 1138年，定都临安；1141年与金议和，次年杀岳飞。

steps.text: 1162: Visits Jiankang after the Jin are repulsed at Caishi, then returns and abdicates to Xiaozong.
steps.text_zh: 1162年，采石大捷后巡幸建康，返临安后禅位孝宗。

steps.text: 1187: Dies in Lin'an after 25 years as retired emperor.
steps.text_zh: 1187年，做了二十五年太上皇后，崩于临安。

title: Han Shizhong's campaigns
summary: From a teenage recruit on the Xixia frontier, Han Shizhong became one of the four great generals of the Southern Song, trapping the Jin fleet at Huangtiandang and holding the Huai line until he was stripped of command.
summary_zh: 韩世忠少年从军抗击西夏，后成为南宋中兴四将之一，黄天荡困金兵、大仪镇破敌、镇守楚州，终被收去兵权，闲居西湖而终。

steps.text: 1089: Born in Yan'an (Suide by some accounts) to a poor family.
steps.text_zh: 1089年，生于延安（一说绥德）贫家。

steps.text: c. 1107: An eighteen-year-old recruit, he scales the walls of Yinzhou against the Xixia and kills its commander.
steps.text_zh: 约1107年，十八岁应募从军，攻西夏银州时率先登城斩将。

steps.text: 1121: Tracks the rebel Fang La to his mountain cave at Bangyuan and captures him.
steps.text_zh: 1121年，随军镇压方腊，深入帮源洞生擒方腊。

steps.text: 1129: Marches on Hangzhou to crush the Miao-Liu mutiny and restore Emperor Gaozong.
steps.text_zh: 1129年，率军进讨苗刘兵变，助高宗复位。

steps.text: 1130: With 8,000 men and his wife Liang Hongyu beating the drums, he bottles up Wuzhu's Jin fleet at Huangtiandang for 48 days.
steps.text_zh: 1130年，以八千水军将金兀术十万大军困于黄天荡四十八日，夫人梁红玉亲自擂鼓助战。

steps.text: 1134: Ambushes the Jin cavalry at Dayi, one of the great victories of the restoration.
steps.text_zh: 1134年，设伏大仪镇大败金军，号称“中兴武功第一”。

steps.text: 1135: Garrisons Chuzhou on the Huai frontier for six years, rebuilding the ruined city with his troops.
steps.text_zh: 1135年，移镇楚州，驻守淮东六年，与士卒同甘苦，重建残破城池。

steps.text: 1141: Recalled to Lin'an and stripped of command; he confronts Qin Hui over Yue Fei's 'perhaps' crime.
steps.text_zh: 1141年，被召回临安收去兵权，当面质问秦桧“莫须有”三字何以服天下。

steps.text: 1151: After a decade riding a donkey by the West Lake and refusing to talk of war, he dies in Lin'an.
steps.text_zh: 1151年，闲居西湖十年，骑驴携酒、绝口不言兵事，卒于临安。

title: Yelü Chucai's travels
summary: A Khitan scholar-official of the Jin, Yelü Chucai joined Genghis Khan after the fall of Zhongdu, followed him to Central Asia, and as Ögedei's chief administrator tried to curb Mongol destruction of northern China.
summary_zh: 契丹贵族耶律楚材原仕金朝，中都陷落后归附成吉思汗，随军西征，窝阔台时主持汉地政务，力阻屠城，奠定元朝治理之基。

steps.text: 1190: Born in Zhongdu, a descendant of the Liao imperial house.
steps.text_zh: 1190年，生于金中都，为辽朝皇族后裔。

steps.text: 1215: Left behind when the Jin court flees south, he witnesses the Mongol capture of Zhongdu and turns to Buddhist study.
steps.text_zh: 1215年，金廷南迁后留守中都，亲历蒙古攻陷中都，此后潜心参禅。

steps.place_zh: 成吉思汗大帐（克鲁伦河畔）
steps.text: 1218: Summoned by Genghis Khan, who is impressed by the tall, long-bearded scholar.
steps.text_zh: 1218年，应成吉思汗召至漠北，以“长髯人”见知。

steps.text: c. 1220: Follows the western campaign and lives in Samarkand, later recording it in his Record of a Journey West.
steps.text_zh: 约1220年，随成吉思汗西征，居寻思干数年，后著《西游录》。

steps.text: 1226: On the Xixia campaign, while others loot, he gathers books and rhubarb, which later saves soldiers from an epidemic.
steps.text_zh: 1226年，随军攻西夏，众将争抢财物，他只取书籍和大黄，后以大黄救治疫病。

steps.text: 1229: Organises the ritual of Ögedei's enthronement and becomes his chief administrator for the Chinese lands.
steps.text_zh: 1229年，为窝阔台即位定礼仪，受命主持汉地政务。

steps.text: 1233: Persuades Ögedei not to massacre the population of the fallen Jin capital.
steps.text_zh: 1233年，汴京城破，力劝窝阔台免于屠城，保全百余万人。

steps.text: 1236: Sets up a bureau for editing classics in Yanjing and argues for taxation instead of fiefs.
steps.text_zh: 1236年，在燕京设编修所，并力主以赋税代替分封。

steps.text: 1244: Sidelined after Ögedei's death, he dies in Karakorum; he is buried near Yanjing.
steps.text_zh: 1244年，窝阔台死后失势，卒于和林，归葬燕京瓮山。

title: Qiu Chuji's journey west
summary: Daoist master Qiu Chuji trained under Wang Chongyang, spent years in mountain retreat, and at seventy crossed Central Asia to counsel Genghis Khan in the Hindu Kush before returning to lead the Quanzhen order from Yanjing.
summary_zh: 全真道士丘处机师从王重阳，隐修磻溪多年，七十余岁应召万里西行，于兴都库什山觐见成吉思汗，归后住持燕京长春宫。

steps.text: 1148: Born in Qixia, Dengzhou.
steps.text_zh: 1148年，生于登州栖霞。

steps.text: 1167: Becomes a disciple of Wang Chongyang, founder of the Quanzhen school.
steps.text_zh: 1167年，在宁海拜王重阳为师，入全真道。

steps.text: 1170: Accompanying his master west, he is with Wang Chongyang when he dies in Bianliang.
steps.text_zh: 1170年，随师西行，王重阳在汴梁逝世。

steps.text: c. 1174: Begins six years of ascetic retreat at Panxi, followed by seven more at Longmen Mountain.
steps.text_zh: 约1174年，隐居磻溪苦修六年，后又入陇州龙门山修道七年。

steps.text: 1188: Summoned to the Jin court by Emperor Shizong.
steps.text_zh: 1188年，应金世宗召至中都。

steps.text: 1219: Turning down Jin and Song invitations, he accepts Genghis Khan's summons delivered by Liu Zhonglu.
steps.text_zh: 1219年，辞金、宋之召，应成吉思汗使臣刘仲禄之请西行。

steps.text: 1221: After crossing the Mongolian steppe and the Altai, he winters in Samarkand.
steps.text_zh: 1221年，穿越漠北、翻越阿尔泰山，于寻思干过冬。

steps.place_zh: 大雪山（阿富汗兴都库什山）
steps.text: 1222: Meets Genghis Khan in the Hindu Kush and advises him to 'revere Heaven and love the people'.
steps.text_zh: 1222年，在大雪山觐见成吉思汗，进言“敬天爱民”、“清心寡欲”。

steps.text: 1227: Back in Yanjing since 1224 at the Changchun Palace (today's White Cloud Temple), he dies there.
steps.text_zh: 1227年，自1224年起住持燕京长春宫（今白云观），卒于此。

title: Guo Shoujing's travels
summary: Astronomer and hydraulic engineer Guo Shoujing restored canals from Ningxia to Dadu, built observatories across the empire and compiled the Shoushi calendar for Kublai Khan.
summary_zh: 天文学家、水利学家郭守敬修复西夏故渠、主持四海测验、编制《授时历》，又开通通惠河，使漕船直抵大都。

steps.text: 1231: Born in Xingtai, raised by his scholar grandfather and later studies under Liu Bingzhong.
steps.text_zh: 1231年，生于邢州，随祖父郭荣读书，后师从刘秉忠。

steps.text: 1262: Presents six water-management proposals to Kublai and is put in charge of the empire's canals.
steps.text_zh: 1262年，在开平面见忽必烈，陈水利六事，受命提举诸路河渠。

steps.text: 1264: Restores the ancient irrigation canals of Ningxia, watering vast farmlands.
steps.text_zh: 1264年，赴西夏故地修复唐徕、汉延等古渠，灌田万顷。

steps.text: 1276: Joins the calendar reform at Dadu and builds new astronomical instruments such as the simplified armilla.
steps.text_zh: 1276年，参与修订历法，在大都创制简仪等天文仪器。

steps.text: 1279: Leads the Survey of the Four Seas, with an observatory at Gaocheng among 27 sites across the empire.
steps.text_zh: 1279年，主持“四海测验”，在告成等二十七处设点观测。

steps.text: 1280: Completes the Shoushi calendar, with a year of 365.2425 days.
1293: His Tonghui Canal opens, bringing grain barges right into Dadu's Jishuitan harbour.
steps.text_zh: 1293年，主持开凿的通惠河竣工，漕船直抵大都积水潭。

steps.text: 1298: Summoned to Shangdu, he warns that a planned channel needs to be much wider; it floods the next year as he predicted.
steps.text_zh: 1298年，奉召至上都议开铁幡竿渠，力言须加宽，未被采纳，次年果遇山洪。

steps.text: 1316: Dies in Dadu, still in office at 86.
steps.text_zh: 1316年，以八十六岁高龄卒于大都，至死未致仕。

title: Zhao Mengfu's travels
summary: A descendant of the Song royal house, Zhao Mengfu took office under Kublai Khan and moved between Dadu and the south, becoming the leading painter and calligrapher of the Yuan.
summary_zh: 宋宗室后裔赵孟頫应召仕元，往来大都与江南之间，官至翰林学士承旨，书画冠绝一代。

steps.text: 1254: Born in Wuxing, an eleventh-generation descendant of the Song founder.
steps.text_zh: 1254年，生于湖州吴兴，为宋太祖第十一世孙。

steps.text: 1287: Recruited by Cheng Jufu, he meets Kublai Khan, who admires his bearing, and takes office in the Ministry of War.
steps.text_zh: 1287年，经程钜夫举荐至大都觐见忽必烈，授兵部郎中。

steps.text: 1292: Deputy governor of Jinan circuit.
steps.text_zh: 1292年，任同知济南路总管府事。

steps.text: 1295: Back in the south, paints Autumn Colours on the Que and Hua Mountains, recalling Jinan's scenery for his friend Zhou Mi.
steps.text_zh: 1295年，南归，为周密作《鹊华秋色图》，追写济南山水。

steps.text: 1299: Supervisor of Confucian schools in Jiangzhe, living in Hangzhou for a decade.
steps.text_zh: 1299年，任江浙等处儒学提举，居杭州约十年。

steps.text: 1310: Summoned to Dadu by the future Emperor Renzong; rises to Hanlin academician by 1316.
steps.text_zh: 1310年，奉召入大都，受仁宗礼遇，1316年官至翰林学士承旨。

steps.text: 1319: Taking his sick wife, the painter Guan Daosheng, home by the Grand Canal; she dies on the boat at Linqing.
steps.text_zh: 1319年，携病中的夫人管道升沿运河南归，管道升卒于临清舟中。

steps.text: 1322: Dies at home in Huzhou.
steps.text_zh: 1322年，卒于湖州家中。

title: Phagpa's travels
summary: A Sakya lama who left Tibet as a boy, Phagpa became Kublai Khan's spiritual teacher, head of Buddhist and Tibetan affairs and creator of the 'Square Script' for the Yuan empire.
summary_zh: 萨迦派高僧八思巴少年随伯父东行，后为忽必烈帝师，统领佛教与吐蕃事务，创制八思巴文，晚年返归萨迦。

steps.text: 1235: Born into the Khön family that leads the Sakya school.
steps.text_zh: 1235年，生于萨迦款氏家族。

steps.text: 1247: Travelling with his uncle Sakya Pandita, he is present at the Liangzhou meeting with the Mongol prince Köden.
steps.text_zh: 1247年，随伯父萨迦班智达东行，参加与阔端的凉州会盟。

steps.text: 1253: Meets Kublai, then preparing his Dali campaign, and becomes his teacher (by some accounts at Liupan Shan).
steps.text_zh: 1253年，在六盘山（一说）谒见正准备南征大理的忽必烈，为其传法授戒。

steps.text: 1260: Having led the Buddhist side in the 1258 debate at Kaiping, he is named State Preceptor when Kublai becomes Great Khan.
steps.text_zh: 1260年，继1258年开平佛道辩论后，忽必烈即汗位，封其为国师。

steps.text: 1265: Returns to Sakya to set up the administration of Tibet under Yuan rule.
steps.text_zh: 1265年，返回萨迦，建立元朝治下的吐蕃行政体制。

steps.text: 1269: Returns to the capital and presents his new script, which Kublai decrees for all official documents; soon named Imperial Preceptor.
steps.text_zh: 1269年，回到大都进献新字，忽必烈诏令颁行，随后晋封帝师。

steps.text: 1277: Back in Tibet, he presides over the great Buddhist assembly at Chumig.
steps.text_zh: 1277年，返藏后在曲弥主持盛大法会。

steps.text: 1280: Dies at Sakya.
steps.text_zh: 1280年，圆寂于萨迦。

title: Wang Dayuan's voyages
summary: Wang Dayuan sailed twice from Quanzhou through Southeast Asia and the Indian Ocean in the 1330s and wrote the Daoyi Zhilüe, a record of nearly a hundred foreign lands. The order of his ports of call is not recorded, so the route here is a reconstruction.
summary_zh: 汪大渊于1330年代两度自泉州出海，遍历南洋与印度洋诸国，著《岛夷志略》记近百个海外地名。其停靠顺序史无明载，此处路线系据书中所记推拟。

steps.text: 1311: Born in Nanchang.
steps.text_zh: 1311年，生于江西南昌。

steps.text: 1330: Not yet twenty, he sets out on his first voyage from Quanzhou, the empire's greatest port.
steps.text_zh: 1330年，未满二十岁，自泉州首次搭乘商船出海。

steps.text: c. 1330: Calls at Champa on the coast of today's central Vietnam.
steps.text_zh: 约1330年，经占城（今越南中部）。

steps.text: c. 1331: Describes Temasek, the earliest Chinese account of Singapore, and its Chinese residents.
steps.text_zh: 约1331年，到单马锡，留下关于新加坡及当地华人的最早中文记载之一。

steps.text: c. 1332: Visits Ceylon and its famous Buddhist sites.
steps.text_zh: 约1332年，到僧加剌（今斯里兰卡）。

steps.text: c. 1333: Reaches the Malabar coast of India, hub of the pepper trade.
steps.text_zh: 约1333年，到古里佛，为印度西南海岸胡椒贸易中心。

steps.text: 1334: Returns to Quanzhou from his first voyage.
steps.text_zh: 1334年，结束首次远航，回到泉州。

steps.text: c. 1337: On his second voyage (1337–39), sails through the islands of Southeast Asia, including Ma-i in the Philippines.
steps.text_zh: 约1337年，第二次出海（1337–1339年），遍历南洋诸岛，记有麻逸（今菲律宾民都洛）。

steps.text: 1349: Writes the Daoyi Zhilüe, first appended to the Quanzhou gazetteer.
steps.text_zh: 1349年，撰成《岛夷志略》，初附于泉州《清源续志》。

steps.text: 1350: Has the book printed separately back home in Nanchang; nothing is known of his later life.
steps.text_zh: 1350年，回南昌将其书单独刊行，此后事迹不详。

title: Zhou Daguan's voyage to Angkor
summary: Zhou Daguan of Wenzhou sailed with a Yuan embassy to Angkor in 1296–97 and wrote The Customs of Cambodia, the only eyewitness account of the Khmer capital at its height.
summary_zh: 温州人周达观于1296—1297年随元使赴真腊，归后撰《真腊风土记》，是关于吴哥王城鼎盛时期唯一的亲历记载。

steps.text: c. 1270: Born in Yongjia, Wenzhou.
steps.text_zh: 约1270年，生于温州永嘉。

steps.text: 1296: Sails from Wenzhou in the second month with the embassy sent by Temür Khan.
steps.text_zh: 1296年二月，随元成宗所遣使团自温州开洋。

steps.text: 1296: Crosses the Seven Isles Sea east of Hainan, a feared stretch of open water.
steps.text_zh: 1296年，经海南岛以东的七洲洋。

steps.text: 1296: Reaches Champa in the third month.
steps.text_zh: 1296年三月，抵达占城。

steps.text: 1296: Calls at Zhenpu on the southern coast before entering the Mekong.
steps.text_zh: 1296年，至真蒲，由此转入湄公河。

steps.text: 1296: Changes to smaller boats at Chanan to cross the Tonle Sap.
steps.text_zh: 1296年，至查南换乘小舟，渡洞里萨湖。

steps.text: 1296: Arrives at Angkor in the seventh month and spends nearly a year observing the Khmer capital.
steps.text_zh: 1296年七月，抵达真腊都城吴哥，居留近一年，详察风土。

steps.text: 1297: Sails home, landing at Siming in the eighth month.
steps.text_zh: 1297年八月，回舟抵达四明。

steps.text: c. 1300: Back home he writes The Customs of Cambodia; little is known of his later life.
steps.text_zh: 约1300年，归乡后撰成《真腊风土记》，晚年事迹不详。

title: Zhu Yuanzhang's rise
summary: From an orphaned peasant and wandering monk, Zhu Yuanzhang joined the Red Turbans at Haozhou, took Nanjing, defeated his rivals and founded the Ming dynasty in 1368.
summary_zh: 朱元璋出身贫农、做过游方僧，投奔濠州红巾军，攻取集庆，鄱阳湖大败陈友谅，1368年建立明朝，定都南京。

steps.text: 1328: Born to a poor tenant family in Zhongli, Haozhou.
steps.text_zh: 1328年，生于濠州钟离贫苦佃农家庭。

steps.text: c. 1345: Orphaned by famine and plague in 1344, he becomes a novice monk and spends three years begging across the Huaixi region.
steps.text_zh: 约1345年，前一年父母兄长死于饥疫，入皇觉寺为僧，云游淮西各地化缘三年。

steps.text: 1352: Joins Guo Zixing's Red Turban army at Haozhou and marries his adopted daughter, later Empress Ma.
steps.text_zh: 1352年，投奔濠州郭子兴红巾军，娶其养女马氏。

steps.text: 1355: After taking Hezhou, he inherits Guo's army and crosses the Yangtze at Caishi.
steps.text_zh: 1355年，据和州，郭子兴死后统其部众，渡江取采石。

steps.text: 1356: Captures Jiqing and renames it Yingtian, making it his base.
steps.text_zh: 1356年，攻占集庆，改名应天府，以此为根据地。

steps.text: 1363: Destroys Chen Youliang's huge fleet with fire ships in a 36-day battle on Poyang Lake.
steps.text_zh: 1363年，鄱阳湖大战三十六日，以火攻大败陈友谅水军。

steps.text: 1368: Proclaims himself emperor of the Ming in Yingtian.
steps.text_zh: 1368年，在应天称帝，建立明朝，年号洪武。

steps.text: 1368: Travels to Kaifeng to direct the northern campaign and weigh it as a capital.
steps.text_zh: 1368年，亲赴汴梁部署北伐，并考察建都之地。

steps.text: 1369: Orders a grand Central Capital built at his birthplace, abandoned six years later.
steps.text_zh: 1369年，诏以家乡临濠为中都，大兴土木，六年后罢建。

steps.text: 1380: Executes Chancellor Hu Weiyong and abolishes the chancellorship.
steps.text_zh: 1380年，诛丞相胡惟庸，废除丞相制度。

steps.text: 1398: Dies in Nanjing and is buried at the Xiaoling mausoleum on Purple Mountain.
steps.text_zh: 1398年，崩于南京，葬钟山孝陵。

title: Zhu Di's campaigns
summary: Born in Nanjing and enfeoffed at Beiping, the Prince of Yan seized the throne in a civil war, moved the capital north to Beijing and died returning from his fifth campaign into Mongolia.
summary_zh: 朱棣生于南京，就藩北平，以“靖难”夺取帝位，迁都北京，五次亲征漠北，最终病逝于北征归途。

steps.text: 1360: Born in Yingtian (Nanjing), fourth son of the rebel leader Zhu Yuanzhang.
steps.text_zh: 1360年，生于应天，是朱元璋第四子。

steps.text: 1380: Takes up his fief as Prince of Yan in Beiping, guarding the northern frontier against the Mongols.
steps.text_zh: 1380年，以燕王身份就藩北平，镇守北疆、防御蒙古。

steps.text: 1399: Facing the Jianwen Emperor's purge of the princes, he rises in revolt under the slogan of 'clearing the emperor's side'.
steps.text_zh: 1399年，建文帝削藩，朱棣以“清君侧”为名在北平起兵，靖难之役爆发。

steps.text: 1400: Suffers his worst defeat at Dongchang at the hands of the loyalist general Sheng Yong.
steps.text_zh: 1400年，在东昌被南军盛庸大败，是靖难中最惨重的失利。

steps.text: 1402: Enters Nanjing as the gates are opened to him and takes the throne as the Yongle Emperor.
steps.text_zh: 1402年，攻入南京，即位称帝，年号永乐。

steps.text: 1410: Leads his first personal campaign north of the Gobi, routing the Mongol khan Bunyashiri on the Onon River.
steps.text_zh: 1410年，首次亲征漠北，在斡难河击败鞑靼本雅失里。

steps.place: Khulan Khushuun (near the Tuul River, Mongolia)
steps.place_zh: 忽兰忽失温（今蒙古国土拉河一带）
steps.text: 1414: On his second campaign he defeats the Oirats at Khulan Khushuun after a hard-fought battle.
steps.text_zh: 1414年，第二次北征，在忽兰忽失温苦战击败瓦剌。

steps.text: 1421: Formally moves the capital to Beijing, where the new Forbidden City has just been completed.
steps.text_zh: 1421年，紫禁城落成，正式迁都北京。

steps.place_zh: 榆木川（今内蒙古多伦一带）
steps.text: 1424: Dies at Yumuchuan on the way back from his fifth campaign against the Mongols.
steps.text_zh: 1424年，第五次北征归途中病逝于榆木川。

title: Yu Qian's life
summary: A Hangzhou native, Yu Qian served as censor and long-time governor in Henan and Shanxi, saved Beijing after the Tumu disaster, and was executed after the restored emperor's coup.
summary_zh: 于谦是杭州人，曾任御史、长期巡抚河南山西；土木之变后力挽狂澜保卫北京，却在夺门之变后被冤杀。

steps.text: 1398: Born in Qiantang (Hangzhou) to a family of scholar-officials.
steps.text_zh: 1398年，生于钱塘（今杭州）的仕宦之家。

steps.text: 1421: Passes the metropolitan examination and becomes a jinshi, the year the capital moves to Beijing.
steps.text_zh: 1421年，考中进士，恰逢明朝迁都北京。

steps.text: 1426: As a censor with the Xuande Emperor's army, he berates the rebel Prince of Han, Zhu Gaoxu, after his surrender.
steps.text_zh: 1426年，以御史随宣德帝平定汉王朱高煦之乱，当面数落其罪，声震一时。

steps.text: 1427: Sent as circuit inspector to Jiangxi, he overturns hundreds of unjust verdicts.
steps.text_zh: 1427年，巡按江西，平反冤狱数百起。

steps.text: 1430: Appointed grand coordinator of Henan and Shanxi, a post he holds for nearly two decades, managing famine relief and Yellow River dykes.
steps.text_zh: 1430年，出任河南、山西巡抚，前后近二十年，赈灾、修河堤，政声卓著。

steps.text: 1440: Still touring Shanxi as governor; he refuses to bring gifts for the eunuch Wang Zhen, saying he brings only 'two sleeves of clear breeze'.
steps.text_zh: 1440年，仍巡抚山西，入京不向权宦王振送礼，留下“两袖清风”的佳话。

steps.text: 1449: After the emperor is captured at Tumu, he opposes moving the capital south and as minister of war repels the Oirat army at the gates of Beijing.
steps.text_zh: 1449年，土木之变后力排南迁之议，以兵部尚书主持北京保卫战，击退瓦剌。

steps.text: 1457: When the deposed Yingzong regains the throne in the Duomen coup, Yu Qian is falsely charged and executed in Beijing.
steps.text_zh: 1457年，夺门之变后英宗复辟，于谦被诬谋逆，在北京遇害。

title: Qi Jiguang's campaigns
summary: From a hereditary military family in Shandong, Qi Jiguang trained the Qi Army that crushed the wokou pirates in Zhejiang and Fujian, then rebuilt the Great Wall defences north of Beijing.
summary_zh: 戚继光出身山东世袭军户，组建“戚家军”在浙闽荡平倭寇，后镇守蓟州、重修长城，晚年罢归蓬莱。

steps.text: 1528: Born at Luqiao near Jining, where his father was serving; the family's hereditary post was at Dengzhou.
steps.text_zh: 1528年，生于父亲任所济宁鲁桥（一说），祖籍登州。

steps.text: 1544: Inherits his father's post as assistant commander of Dengzhou Guard, guarding the Shandong coast.
steps.text_zh: 1544年，承袭登州卫指挥佥事，负责山东海防。

steps.text: 1559: Posted to Zhejiang against the pirates, he recruits miners and farmers of Yiwu and drills them into the 'Qi Army'.
steps.text_zh: 1559年，调任浙江抗倭，在义乌招募矿工农民，练成“戚家军”。

steps.text: 1561: Wins nine straight battles around Taizhou, breaking the main wokou raids on Zhejiang.
steps.text_zh: 1561年，台州九战九捷，基本肃清浙江倭患。

steps.text: 1562: Marches into Fujian and storms the pirate stronghold on Hengyu island across the tidal flats.
steps.text_zh: 1562年，入闽抗倭，涉滩奇袭横屿倭巢。

steps.text: 1563: With Yu Dayou and Liu Xian, he recaptures Xinghua prefecture and wins at Pinghaiwei.
steps.text_zh: 1563年，与俞大猷、刘显合兵，收复兴化府，取得平海卫大捷。

steps.text: 1568: Transferred north to command the Jizhou garrison, he builds hollow watchtowers along the Great Wall and keeps the Mongols at bay for sixteen years.
steps.text_zh: 1568年，北调总理蓟州练兵，沿长城修筑空心敌台，镇守十六年边境无事。

steps.text: 1583: After Zhang Juzheng's death his patrons fall, and he is shunted off to command in Guangdong.
steps.text_zh: 1583年，张居正死后失去倚靠，被调往广东任总兵。

steps.text: 1588: Dismissed in 1585, he dies at home in Penglai, poor and ill.
steps.text_zh: 1588年，罢官回乡三年后，在蓬莱贫病而终。

title: Hai Rui's career
summary: From Hainan Island, the famously incorruptible Hai Rui rose from county posts to denounce the Jiajing Emperor, governed Jiangnan briefly, and died in office in Nanjing.
summary_zh: 海瑞出身海南，从县学教谕、知县做起，以死谏嘉靖帝闻名天下，曾短暂巡抚江南，最终病逝于南京任上。

steps.text: 1514: Born in Qiongshan on Hainan Island; his father dies when he is three and his mother raises him strictly.
steps.text_zh: 1514年，生于海南琼山，幼年丧父，由母亲严格教养。

steps.text: 1549: Passes the Guangdong provincial examination; he will never pass the higher metropolitan exam.
steps.text_zh: 1549年，考中广东乡试举人，此后会试不第。

steps.text: 1554: Becomes county instructor at Nanping and refuses to kneel to visiting censors.
steps.text_zh: 1554年，任福建南平县教谕，见上官不跪，人称“笔架博士”。

steps.text: 1558: As magistrate of Chun'an he plants his own vegetables and stands up to the governor-general's son.
steps.text_zh: 1558年，任淳安知县，自种菜蔬，敢于惩治总督胡宗宪之子。

steps.text: 1562: Transferred to be magistrate of Xingguo in Jiangxi.
steps.text_zh: 1562年，调任江西兴国知县。

steps.text: 1566: As a Ministry of Revenue official he buys a coffin and submits a memorial denouncing the Jiajing Emperor; he is jailed until the emperor dies.
steps.text_zh: 1566年，任户部主事，备好棺材上《治安疏》直斥嘉靖帝，被下狱，帝崩后获释。

steps.text: 1569: As grand coordinator of Yingtian, based in Suzhou, he forces great landlords to return seized land and dredges the Wusong River.
steps.text_zh: 1569年，巡抚应天十府，驻苏州，逼豪强退田，疏浚吴淞江。

steps.text: 1570: Impeached by the powerful families, he retires to Hainan for some fifteen years.
steps.text_zh: 1570年，遭弹劾罢官，回海南闲居十余年。

steps.text: 1587: Recalled in 1585 to Nanjing as chief censor, he dies in office there, leaving barely enough money for his funeral.
steps.text_zh: 1587年，于1585年起复后任南京右都御史，卒于任上，身后几无余财。

title: Zhang Juzheng's life
summary: A prodigy from Jiangling in Hubei, Zhang Juzheng rose through the Hanlin Academy to become senior grand secretary, pushing through the Wanli reforms before dying in power in Beijing.
summary_zh: 张居正是湖北江陵神童，经翰林院入阁，任首辅十年主持万历新政，死于北京任上，身后遭清算。

steps.text: 1525: Born in Jiangling, Huguang, to a modest family of military registry.
steps.text_zh: 1525年，生于湖广江陵。

steps.text: 1540: Passes the Huguang provincial examination at fifteen, having been held back three years earlier by an examiner who thought him too young.
steps.text_zh: 1540年，十五岁中湖广乡试举人；此前巡抚顾璘有意让他晚三年及第以磨砺其才。

steps.text: 1547: Becomes a jinshi and enters the Hanlin Academy.
steps.text_zh: 1547年，考中进士，选为庶吉士入翰林院。

steps.text: 1554: Takes sick leave and spends three years at home, studying local conditions.
steps.text_zh: 1554年，告病回乡，在江陵住了三年，留心民间疾苦。

steps.text: 1567: Enters the Grand Secretariat under the new Longqing Emperor.
steps.text_zh: 1567年，隆庆帝即位，张居正入阁参与机务。

steps.text: 1573: As senior grand secretary and regent-like tutor to the child Wanli Emperor, launches reforms of officials' performance reviews and finances.
steps.text_zh: 1573年，以首辅辅佐少年万历帝，推行考成法，整顿吏治财政。

steps.text: 1578: Returns home in grand state to bury his father, after the controversy over his not observing full mourning.
steps.text_zh: 1578年，因“夺情”风波后回江陵葬父，排场盛大。

steps.text: 1582: Dies in Beijing after nationwide land surveys and the Single Whip tax reform; within two years his family is disgraced.
steps.text_zh: 1582年，推行清丈田亩与一条鞭法后病逝于北京，身后不久即被抄家。

title: Li Shizhen's travels
summary: A doctor's son from Qizhou in Hubei, Li Shizhen gave up the examinations for medicine, served briefly at court and travelled widely collecting herbs for his great Compendium of Materia Medica.
summary_zh: 李时珍是蕲州医家之子，弃科举而从医，曾短暂入太医院，遍访名山采药，历时近三十年写成《本草纲目》。

steps.text: 1518: Born in Qizhou into a family of physicians.
steps.text_zh: 1518年，生于蕲州一个世医之家。

steps.text: 1551: After failing the provincial exam in Wuchang three times, he turns to medicine and is engaged by the Prince of Chu there.
steps.text_zh: 1551年，此前三次赴武昌乡试落第，转而专心行医，被楚王聘为王府奉祠正。

steps.text: c. 1556: Recommended to the Imperial Medical Academy in Beijing, where he reads rare herbals but leaves after about a year.
steps.text_zh: 约1556年，被荐入北京太医院，饱览珍本医书，约一年后辞归。

steps.text: c. 1565: Begins collecting trips to the mountains; on Wudang he studies the medicinal plants of the Daoist temples.
steps.text_zh: 约1565年，开始外出采药考察，登武当山。

steps.text: c. 1566: Gathers specimens on Mount Lu in Jiangxi, by traditional accounts.
steps.text_zh: 约1566年，据传在江西庐山采集药材标本。

steps.text: c. 1568: Continues on to Mount Mao and the hills near Nanjing, questioning farmers, hunters and fishermen.
steps.text_zh: 约1568年，又至茅山、南京牛首山一带，向农夫、猎人、渔民求教。

steps.text: 1578: Completes the Compendium of Materia Medica after nearly thirty years and three major revisions.
steps.text_zh: 1578年，历时近三十年、三易其稿，完成《本草纲目》。

steps.text: 1580: Visits the literary giant Wang Shizhen in Taicang to ask for a preface.
steps.text_zh: 1580年，赴太仓拜访文坛领袖王世贞，求序。

steps.text: 1590: Wang Shizhen's preface arrives and the Nanjing printer Hu Chenglong begins carving the blocks.
steps.text_zh: 1590年，王世贞作序，南京书商胡承龙开始刻印《本草纲目》。

steps.text: 1593: Dies at home in Qizhou, before the printed book appears.
steps.text_zh: 1593年，病逝于蕲州，未及见到书籍刊成。

title: Tang Xianzu's life
summary: The dramatist of The Peony Pavilion refused to court the powerful, served in Nanjing, was banished to the tip of Guangdong, governed a small Zhejiang county and retired home to write.
summary_zh: 汤显祖不肯依附权贵，仕途坎坷：任职南京，被贬雷州半岛，出任遂昌知县，最后弃官回临川专心写戏。

steps.text: 1550: Born in Linchuan, Jiangxi, into a scholarly family.
steps.text_zh: 1550年，生于江西临川书香门第。

steps.text: 1570: Passes the Jiangxi provincial examination at twenty.
steps.text_zh: 1570年，二十岁中江西乡试举人。

steps.text: 1583: Having twice refused Zhang Juzheng's invitations to befriend his sons and failed the exams, he finally passes after Zhang's death.
steps.text_zh: 1583年，此前两次拒绝张居正拉拢而落第，张死后方中进士。

steps.text: 1584: Takes minor posts in the secondary capital, Nanjing, rising to secretary in the Ministry of Rites.
steps.text_zh: 1584年，赴南京任太常寺博士，后升礼部主事。

steps.text: 1591: On his way into exile he passes Xiangshan'ao (Macau) and writes poems on its foreign merchants.
steps.text_zh: 1591年，贬谪途中经过香山澳，写诗记述葡萄牙商人。

steps.text: 1591: Banished as a petty clerk to Xuwen at the tip of the Leizhou Peninsula for a memorial attacking the grand secretaries.
steps.text_zh: 1591年，上《论辅臣科臣疏》触怒皇帝，被贬为徐闻典史。

steps.text: 1593: As magistrate of Suichang he runs a lenient administration, even letting prisoners home for the New Year.
steps.text_zh: 1593年，任遂昌知县，施政宽仁，曾在除夕放囚犯回家过年。

steps.text: 1598: Resigns and goes home, where he completes The Peony Pavilion.
steps.text_zh: 1598年，弃官归里，完成《牡丹亭》。

steps.text: 1616: Dies in Linchuan, the same year as Shakespeare.
steps.text_zh: 1616年，卒于临川，与莎士比亚同年去世。

title: Matteo Ricci's journey
summary: An Italian Jesuit, Ricci sailed via Goa to Macau, then worked his way north through Guangdong, Jiangxi and Nanjing to become the first missionary allowed to live in Beijing.
summary_zh: 意大利耶稣会士利玛窦经果阿到澳门，自广东北上，历经韶州、南昌、南京，终获准定居北京，传播西学。

steps.text: 1552: Born in Macerata in the Papal States.
steps.text_zh: 1552年，生于教皇国马切拉塔。

steps.text: 1571: Joins the Society of Jesus in Rome and studies mathematics under Christopher Clavius.
steps.text_zh: 1571年，在罗马加入耶稣会，师从数学家克拉维乌斯。

steps.text: 1578: Sails from Lisbon to Portuguese Goa, where he teaches and is ordained.
steps.text_zh: 1578年，自里斯本远航至果阿，在此任教并晋铎。

steps.text: 1582: Arrives in Macau and begins learning Chinese.
steps.text_zh: 1582年，抵达澳门，开始学习汉语。

steps.text: 1583: With Michele Ruggieri he settles in Zhaoqing, where he draws his first Chinese world map.
steps.text_zh: 1583年，与罗明坚获准定居肇庆，绘制首幅中文世界地图。

steps.text: 1589: Expelled from Zhaoqing, he moves to Shaozhou and switches from Buddhist robes to the dress of a Confucian scholar.
steps.text_zh: 1589年，被逐出肇庆，转居韶州，后改穿儒服。

steps.text: 1595: After failing to stay in Nanjing he settles in Nanchang and writes On Friendship.
steps.text_zh: 1595年，赴南京未成，转居南昌，著《交友论》。

steps.text: 1599: Settles in Nanjing and meets leading scholars, soon including Xu Guangqi.
steps.text_zh: 1599年，定居南京，结交士大夫，次年结识徐光启。

steps.text: 1601: Reaches Beijing and presents clocks and a clavichord to the Wanli Emperor, who lets him stay.
steps.text_zh: 1601年，进京向万历帝进献自鸣钟、西琴等，获准留居北京。

steps.text: 1610: Dies in Beijing after publishing his great world map and the Chinese Euclid; the emperor grants a burial plot.
steps.text_zh: 1610年，在刊印《坤舆万国全图》、合译《几何原本》后病逝北京，获赐葬地。

title: Xu Guangqi's life
summary: A Shanghai scholar who met the Jesuits in Guangdong and Nanjing, Xu Guangqi translated Euclid with Ricci, experimented with crops in Shanghai and Tianjin, and ended as a grand secretary reforming the calendar.
summary_zh: 徐光启是上海人，在韶州、南京结识传教士，与利玛窦合译《几何原本》，在上海、天津试验农作物，晚年官至大学士，主持修订历法。

steps.text: 1562: Born in Shanghai county to a family of small merchants and farmers.
steps.text_zh: 1562年，生于上海县一个小商兼农之家。

steps.text: 1595: Working as a tutor in Shaozhou, he meets the Jesuit Lazzaro Cattaneo, his first contact with Christianity.
steps.text_zh: 1595年，在韶州教书，结识耶稣会士郭居静，首次接触天主教。

steps.text: 1597: Tops the Shuntian provincial examination in Beijing.
steps.text_zh: 1597年，在北京顺天府乡试中考取第一名。

steps.text: 1603: Having met Ricci here in 1600, he is baptized in Nanjing as Paul.
steps.text_zh: 1603年，三年前在此结识利玛窦，此年在南京受洗，教名保禄。

steps.text: 1606: A jinshi since 1604, he translates the first six books of Euclid's Elements with Ricci, published in 1607.
steps.text_zh: 1606年，中进士后入翰林，与利玛窦合译《几何原本》前六卷，次年刊行。

steps.text: 1607: Returns home to mourn his father and experiments with sweet potatoes and other crops.
steps.text_zh: 1607年，回乡守父丧，试种番薯等作物。

steps.text: 1613: Opens farms near Tianjin to test rice growing and irrigation in the north.
steps.text_zh: 1613年，在天津垦田，试验北方种稻和水利。

steps.text: 1629: Placed in charge of reforming the calendar with Jesuit astronomers, producing the Chongzhen Calendar.
steps.text_zh: 1629年，奉命主持修订历法，与传教士合编《崇祯历书》。

steps.text: 1633: Dies in Beijing as a grand secretary; he is later buried at Xujiahui in Shanghai.
steps.text_zh: 1633年，以大学士身份病逝于北京，后归葬上海徐家汇。

title: Yuan Chonghuan's campaigns
summary: A southerner with a passion for frontier affairs, Yuan Chonghuan built Ningyuan into the bulwark that stopped Nurhaci, but was executed after the Manchus outflanked him to reach Beijing.
summary_zh: 袁崇焕生于广东，好谈兵事，坚守宁远击退努尔哈赤，却在后金绕道兵临北京后被崇祯帝凌迟处死。

steps.text: 1584: Born in Dongguan, Guangdong (some accounts say he grew up in Teng county, Guangxi).
steps.text_zh: 1584年，生于广东东莞（一说广西藤县）。

steps.text: 1619: Becomes a jinshi and is posted as magistrate of Shaowu, where he spends his time talking strategy with veterans.
steps.text_zh: 1619年，中进士，任福建邵武知县，常与老兵谈论边事。

steps.text: 1622: After the loss of Guangning he rides alone to inspect the pass and volunteers to defend Liaodong.
steps.text_zh: 1622年，广宁失守后单骑出关考察形势，自请守辽。

steps.text: 1626: Defends the walls he had rebuilt at Ningyuan with Portuguese-style cannon and repulses Nurhaci.
steps.text_zh: 1626年，凭借亲手修筑的宁远城和西洋大炮击退努尔哈赤。

steps.text: 1627: Holds the Ningyuan–Jinzhou line against Hong Taiji, then resigns under attack from Wei Zhongxian's faction.
steps.text_zh: 1627年，宁锦大捷挡住皇太极，却遭魏忠贤党羽排挤去职。

steps.text: 1627: Returns home to Guangdong.
steps.text_zh: 1627年，辞官回乡。

steps.text: 1629: Recalled by the Chongzhen Emperor, he summons the island commander Mao Wenlong to Shuangdao and executes him.
steps.text_zh: 1629年，被崇祯帝起用为蓟辽督师，于双岛诱斩东江总兵毛文龙。

steps.text: 1629: When Hong Taiji outflanks the Liaodong line, he races to Beijing's defence but is arrested on suspicion of treason.
steps.text_zh: 1629年，皇太极绕道入关，袁崇焕驰援京师，反被疑通敌下狱。

steps.text: 1630: Executed by slicing in Beijing; he is rehabilitated only by the Qianlong Emperor.
steps.text_zh: 1630年，在北京被凌迟处死，直到乾隆时才平反。

title: Li Zicheng's campaigns
summary: A laid-off postal courier from northern Shaanxi, Li Zicheng became the 'Dashing King' of the peasant rebels, took Beijing and ended the Ming, but was crushed by the Qing within a year.
summary_zh: 李自成本是陕北驿卒，起事后号称“闯王”，转战中原，攻破北京灭亡明朝，但不到一年便被清军击败身死。

steps.text: 1606: Born in Mizhi in drought-stricken northern Shaanxi; he later works as a postal courier.
steps.text_zh: 1606年，生于陕北米脂，后为银川驿驿卒。

steps.text: 1638: After a crushing defeat near Tongguan, he hides in the Shangluo mountains with a handful of followers.
steps.text_zh: 1638年，在潼关南原惨败，仅率十余骑隐入商洛山中。

steps.text: 1641: Takes Luoyang, kills the Prince of Fu and distributes his grain, with the slogan 'equal land, no taxes'.
steps.text_zh: 1641年，攻克洛阳，杀福王，开仓济民，提出“均田免赋”。

steps.text: 1642: Besieges Kaifeng for the third time; the Yellow River dykes are breached and the city drowns.
steps.text_zh: 1642年，三围开封，黄河决堤，全城被淹。

steps.text: 1643: Makes Xiangyang his base and proclaims himself 'New Shun King'.
steps.text_zh: 1643年，以襄阳为据点，自称“新顺王”。

steps.text: 1643: Defeats the last Ming field army under Sun Chuanting at Tongguan and enters Shaanxi.
steps.text_zh: 1643年，在潼关击败孙传庭，进入关中。

steps.text: 1644: Proclaims the Shun dynasty in Xi'an at the lunar New Year.
steps.text_zh: 1644年正月，在西安建国号“大顺”。

steps.text: 1644: Takes Beijing; the Chongzhen Emperor hangs himself on Coal Hill.
steps.text_zh: 1644年，攻入北京，崇祯帝自缢于煤山，明朝灭亡。

steps.text: 1644: Routed at Shanhai Pass by Wu Sangui and the Qing army, he abandons Beijing.
steps.text_zh: 1644年，在山海关被吴三桂与清军击溃，被迫退出北京。

steps.text: 1645: Dies at Mount Jiugong in Hubei while fleeing south, killed by local militia by most accounts.
steps.text_zh: 1645年，南撤途中殒命湖北九宫山，一般认为死于当地乡勇之手。

title: Shi Kefa's life
summary: A disciple of the Donglin martyr Zuo Guangdou, Shi Kefa fought rebels across central China, became the Southern Ming's chief minister, and died defending Yangzhou against the Qing.
summary_zh: 史可法是东林名臣左光斗的门生，曾转战江淮镇压农民军，南明时督师江北，最终死守扬州殉国。

steps.text: 1601: Born in Xiangfu (Kaifeng), Henan, to a family registered in Daxing near Beijing.
steps.text_zh: 1601年，生于河南祥符，祖籍顺天大兴。

steps.text: 1625: Disguised as a cleaner, he visits his tortured teacher Zuo Guangdou in prison, who sends him away to save himself for the country.
steps.text_zh: 1625年，乔装入狱探望受酷刑的老师左光斗，被其怒斥离去以图报国。

steps.text: 1629: A jinshi of 1628, he is posted as judicial officer of Xi'an prefecture.
steps.text_zh: 1629年，前一年中进士，授西安府推官。

steps.text: 1637: As grand coordinator of Anqing and neighbouring prefectures, he fights the roving rebel armies.
steps.text_zh: 1637年，巡抚安庆、庐州等府，与农民军作战。

steps.text: 1641: Becomes director-general of grain transport on the Grand Canal at Huai'an.
steps.text_zh: 1641年，任漕运总督，驻淮安。

steps.text: 1644: After the fall of Beijing he helps set up the Hongguang court in Nanjing, but is edged out by Ma Shiying.
steps.text_zh: 1644年，北京陷落后参与拥立弘光政权，旋遭马士英排挤。

steps.text: 1644: Goes to Yangzhou as commander of the four northern garrisons, trying to hold the line of the Huai.
steps.text_zh: 1644年，出镇扬州，督师江北四镇。

steps.text: 1645: Refuses to surrender to the Qing; Yangzhou falls after a short siege and he is killed, followed by the ten-day massacre.
steps.text_zh: 1645年，拒绝降清，扬州城破殉国，清军随即屠城十日。

title: Koxinga's life
summary: Born in Japan to a Chinese pirate-merchant and a Japanese mother, Zheng Chenggong fought for the Ming from Xiamen, failed before Nanjing, and drove the Dutch from Taiwan shortly before his death.
summary_zh: 郑成功生于日本平户，父为海商郑芝龙。他以厦门为基地抗清复明，北伐南京失利后，率军收复台湾，不久病逝。

steps.text: 1624: Born in Hirado, Japan, to Zheng Zhilong and a Japanese mother of the Tagawa family.
steps.text_zh: 1624年，生于日本平户，父郑芝龙，母田川氏。

steps.text: 1630: Brought to his father's base at Anping in Fujian to receive a Chinese education.
steps.text_zh: 1630年，被接回福建安平，读书应举。

steps.text: 1644: Studies at the Imperial Academy in Nanjing under Qian Qianyi.
steps.text_zh: 1644年，入南京国子监，师从钱谦益。

steps.text: 1645: The Longwu Emperor in Fuzhou grants him the imperial surname Zhu, hence 'Koxinga' (Lord of the Imperial Surname).
steps.text_zh: 1645年，隆武帝在福州赐其国姓“朱”，人称“国姓爷”。

steps.text: 1646: When his father surrenders to the Qing and his mother dies, he burns his scholar's robes and raises troops on Nan'ao.
steps.text_zh: 1646年，父亲降清、母亲殉难，他焚儒服，在南澳募兵抗清。

steps.text: 1650: Seizes Xiamen and makes it the base of his maritime empire.
steps.text_zh: 1650年，夺取厦门，作为抗清基地。

steps.text: 1659: Sails up the Yangtze and besieges Nanjing, but is routed by a surprise Qing sortie.
steps.text_zh: 1659年，率大军溯长江而上围攻南京，因轻敌被清军击败。

steps.text: 1661: Assembles his fleet at Penghu on the way to Dutch-held Taiwan.
steps.text_zh: 1661年，率舰队经澎湖，渡海东征台湾。

steps.text: 1661: Lands at Luermen on a high tide and besieges the Dutch in Fort Zeelandia.
steps.text_zh: 1661年，乘涨潮从鹿耳门登陆，围困荷兰人的热兰遮城。

steps.text: 1662: The Dutch surrender Taiwan; a few months later he dies suddenly in Tainan.
steps.text_zh: 1662年，荷兰人投降，台湾收复；数月后郑成功在台南病逝。

title: Li Zhi's life
summary: The iconoclastic thinker Li Zhi served in minor posts from Henan to Yunnan, then retired to a Buddhist cloister in Hubei to write, until he was arrested near Beijing and died in prison.
summary_zh: 思想家李贽历官河南、南京、北京、云南，后弃官寓居湖北麻城著书讲学，以“异端”自居，最终在北京狱中自刎。

steps.text: 1527: Born in Jinjiang, Quanzhou, to a family with a history of overseas trade and Muslim ancestry.
steps.text_zh: 1527年，生于泉州晋江，祖上经营海外贸易，有回族血统。

steps.text: 1552: Passes the Fujian provincial examination, then declines to try for the jinshi.
steps.text_zh: 1552年，中福建乡试举人，此后不再应会试。

steps.text: 1556: Becomes county instructor at Gongcheng in Henan.
steps.text_zh: 1556年，任河南共城县教谕。

steps.text: 1560: Appointed an erudite of the Imperial Academy in Nanjing.
steps.text_zh: 1560年，任南京国子监博士。

steps.text: 1566: Serves in the Ministry of Rites in Beijing, where he discovers the philosophy of Wang Yangming.
steps.text_zh: 1566年，任北京礼部司务，开始接触阳明心学。

steps.text: 1570: Returns to Nanjing as a secretary in the Ministry of Justice and befriends Geng Dingxiang and Jiao Hong.
steps.text_zh: 1570年，任南京刑部员外郎，结识耿定向、焦竑等人。

steps.text: 1577: Serves three years as prefect of remote Yao'an in Yunnan, his last official post.
steps.text_zh: 1577年，出任云南姚安知府，三年后辞官。

steps.text: 1581: Lives with the Geng family in Huang'an, teaching their children.
steps.text_zh: 1581年，寓居黄安耿家，教授子弟。

steps.text: 1585: Moves to Macheng and later lives at the Zhifoyuan cloister by Longtan lake, shaving his head and writing A Book to Burn.
steps.text_zh: 1585年，移居麻城，后住龙湖芝佛院，落发著书，刊行《焚书》。

steps.text: 1601: After his cloister is burned by local officials, his friend Ma Jinglun shelters him in Tongzhou.
steps.text_zh: 1601年，芝佛院被焚后，由友人马经纶接往通州居住。

steps.text: 1602: Arrested for 'spreading heresy', he cuts his throat in prison in Beijing at the age of seventy-five.
steps.text_zh: 1602年，以“敢倡乱道，惑世诬民”罪被捕，在北京狱中以剃刀自刎。

title: Gu Yanwu's travels
summary: After resisting the Qing in Jiangnan, the scholar Gu Yanwu spent his last twenty-five years travelling the north on horseback, studying geography and history, and refused every invitation to serve the new dynasty.
summary_zh: 顾炎武在江南参加抗清，失败后北上游历二十余年，考察山川形势、著书立说，始终拒绝出仕清朝。

steps.text: 1613: Born in Qiandeng, Kunshan, and adopted by his widowed aunt-in-law, Lady Wang.
steps.text_zh: 1613年，生于昆山千灯镇，过继给守节的王氏为嗣。

steps.text: 1644: Appointed a minor official in the Ministry of War of the Southern Ming court in Nanjing.
steps.text_zh: 1644年，被南明弘光朝廷授兵部司务。

steps.text: 1645: Joins the defence of Kunshan; after it falls, his adoptive mother starves herself, charging him never to serve the Qing.
steps.text_zh: 1645年，参加昆山抗清，城破后嗣母绝食殉国，遗命不得仕清。

steps.text: 1657: Leaves Jiangnan for good and begins travelling in Shandong.
steps.text_zh: 1657年，离开江南北上，游历山东。

steps.text: 1659: Makes the first of several pilgrimages to the Ming imperial tombs north of Beijing.
steps.text_zh: 1659年，首次拜谒昌平明十三陵，此后多次往谒。

steps.text: 1663: Visits the Ming loyalist scholar and physician Fu Shan in Taiyuan.
steps.text_zh: 1663年，在太原拜访遗民学者傅山。

steps.text: 1668: Imprisoned in Jinan for months over a literary inquisition case before friends secure his release.
steps.text_zh: 1668年，受黄培诗案牵连，在济南入狱半年，经友人营救获释。

steps.text: 1671: Staying with his nephews in Beijing, he rejects an invitation to help compile the official Ming History.
steps.text_zh: 1671年，在京寓居外甥徐乾学处，坚拒参修《明史》。

steps.text: 1679: Settles at Huayin below Mount Hua, valuing the strategic heart of Guanzhong.
steps.text_zh: 1679年，定居华山脚下的华阴。

steps.text: 1682: Dies after a fall from his horse in Quwo, Shanxi.
steps.text_zh: 1682年，在山西曲沃上马失足，不久去世。

title: Huang Zongxi's life
summary: Son of a Donglin martyr, Huang Zongxi avenged his father in Beijing, fought for the Ming after 1644, and spent his later decades writing and teaching in eastern Zhejiang.
summary_zh: 黄宗羲是东林党人黄尊素之子，曾入京为父讼冤，明亡后起兵抗清，晚年在浙东著书讲学，写成《明夷待访录》。

steps.text: 1610: Born in Yuyao, son of the Donglin official Huang Zunsu.
steps.text_zh: 1610年，生于浙江余姚，父为东林名士黄尊素。

steps.text: 1628: Goes to Beijing to seek justice for his father, who died in prison in 1626, and attacks one of the culprits with an awl in court.
steps.text_zh: 1628年，入京为死于诏狱的父亲讼冤，在会审时以铁锥刺伤仇人许显纯。

steps.text: 1638: Joins the Restoration Society in Nanjing in denouncing the Wei Zhongxian partisan Ruan Dacheng.
steps.text_zh: 1638年，在南京与复社诸生联名发布《留都防乱公揭》，声讨阮大铖。

steps.text: 1645: Raises a 'Loyal Army' of local men and joins the Prince of Lu's resistance at Shaoxing.
steps.text_zh: 1645年，组织“世忠营”，投奔绍兴的鲁王监国政权抗清。

steps.text: 1646: After the defeat he holds out in the Siming Mountains.
steps.text_zh: 1646年，兵败后入四明山结寨坚守。

steps.text: 1649: By some accounts sails to Nagasaki to seek Japanese help for the Ming cause.
steps.text_zh: 1649年，一说曾随使赴日本长崎乞师。

steps.text: 1663: Writes Waiting for the Dawn, a sweeping critique of absolute monarchy.
steps.text_zh: 1663年，写成《明夷待访录》，批判君主专制。

steps.text: 1668: Founds the Zhengren Academy in Ningbo, training a generation of eastern Zhejiang historians.
steps.text_zh: 1668年，在宁波创办甬上证人书院，培养了浙东史学一代学人。

steps.text: 1676: Lectures for several years at Haichang, while compiling the Case Studies of Ming Confucians.
steps.text_zh: 1676年，赴海昌讲学数年，同时编撰《明儒学案》。

steps.text: 1695: Dies at home in Yuyao, asking to be buried without a coffin.
steps.text_zh: 1695年，卒于余姚，遗命薄葬不用棺椁。

title: Xu Wei's life
summary: The eccentric painter, poet and dramatist Xu Wei served as secretary to the anti-pirate commander Hu Zongxian, fell into madness and prison after Hu's fall, and died poor in Shaoxing.
summary_zh: 怪才徐渭能诗善画、工于戏曲，曾入胡宗宪幕府抗倭，胡倒台后精神失常、杀妻入狱，晚年潦倒，卒于故乡绍兴。

steps.text: 1521: Born in Shanyin (Shaoxing) to a concubine; his father dies within months.
steps.text_zh: 1521年，生于山阴，生母为婢妾，出生百日父亲去世。

steps.text: 1542: Having married into the Pan family, he follows his father-in-law to his post in Yangjiang, Guangdong.
steps.text_zh: 1542年，入赘潘家，随岳父赴广东阳江任所。

steps.text: 1557: Joins Hu Zongxian's headquarters as a secretary, drafting memorials and planning campaigns against the pirates.
steps.text_zh: 1557年，入浙闽总督胡宗宪幕府，代拟奏章、参谋抗倭军务。

steps.text: 1566: After Hu's arrest he falls into madness, attempts suicide repeatedly, kills his wife and spends seven years in prison.
steps.text_zh: 1566年，胡宗宪下狱后精神失常，屡次自杀未遂，后误杀继妻，入狱七年。

steps.text: 1576: Released through friends, he travels to the northern frontier at Xuanhua as a guest of governor Wu Dui.
steps.text_zh: 1576年，出狱后应宣府巡抚吴兑之邀北上宣化游幕。

steps.text: 1580: Lives in Beijing with his rescuer Zhang Yuanbian, but chafes at etiquette and soon leaves.
steps.text_zh: 1580年，入京依附张元忭，因不耐礼法拘束，不久南归。

steps.text: 1593: Dies in poverty in Shaoxing, selling his paintings and books to survive.
steps.text_zh: 1593年，在绍兴贫病而终，晚年靠卖书画度日。

title: Kangxi Emperor's travels
summary: The longest-reigning Qing emperor seized power from his regent, toured the south and the northeast, led armies into Mongolia against Galdan and built the summer retreat at Chengde.
summary_zh: 康熙帝亲政后擒拿鳌拜，多次东巡、南巡，三次亲征噶尔丹，修建承德避暑山庄，在位六十一年。

steps.text: 1654: Born Xuanye in the Forbidden City, third son of the Shunzhi Emperor; he takes the throne at seven in 1661.
steps.text_zh: 1654年，生于紫禁城景仁宫，名玄烨；1661年八岁登基。

steps.text: 1669: At fifteen he has the overbearing regent Oboi seized by young wrestlers and takes personal power.
steps.text_zh: 1669年，以布库少年擒拿鳌拜，开始亲政。

steps.text: 1682: On an eastern tour to the Manchu homeland he inspects Jilin and prepares to confront Russian settlers on the Amur.
steps.text_zh: 1682年，东巡盛京，至吉林乌拉，部署抗击沙俄。

steps.text: 1684: Kneels at the Temple of Confucius in Qufu on his first southern tour.
steps.text_zh: 1684年，首次南巡途中在曲阜孔庙行三跪九叩礼。

steps.text: 1684: Visits Nanjing and sacrifices at the Ming founder's tomb, courting southern scholars.
steps.text_zh: 1684年，南巡至江宁，亲祭明孝陵以笼络江南士人。

steps.text: 1691: Receives the Khalkha Mongol princes at Dolon Nor, bringing Outer Mongolia under Qing rule.
steps.text_zh: 1691年，在多伦会盟喀尔喀蒙古诸部，外蒙古归附清朝。
