steps.text: 1696: Personally leads the central army to the Kherlen while his general Fiyanggu crushes Galdan at Jao Modo.
steps.text_zh: 1696年，亲率中路军进抵克鲁伦河，西路费扬古在昭莫多大败噶尔丹。

steps.text: 1697: Campaigns a third time from Ningxia; Galdan dies the same spring.
steps.text_zh: 1697年，第三次亲征，驻跸宁夏，噶尔丹随即败亡。

steps.text: 1703: Begins building the Mountain Resort at Rehe, his summer base for hunting and Mongol diplomacy.
steps.text_zh: 1703年，开始营建热河避暑山庄，作为秋狝、会见蒙古王公之所。

steps.text: 1722: Dies at the Changchun Garden in western Beijing after a 61-year reign.
steps.text_zh: 1722年，崩于北京畅春园，在位六十一年。

title: Qianlong Emperor's travels
summary: Qianlong ruled the Qing at its height, touring Manchuria, Wutai, Shandong and Jiangnan, receiving envoys at Chengde, and abdicating only to keep power until his death.
summary_zh: 乾隆帝统治清朝鼎盛时期，多次东巡、西巡五台、六下江南，在承德接见班禅和英国使团，禅位后仍以太上皇训政至死。

steps.text: 1711: Born Hongli in Prince Yong's mansion, the later Yonghe Temple (some say at Chengde).
steps.text_zh: 1711年，生于雍亲王府（今雍和宫），名弘历（一说生于承德）。

steps.text: 1743: Makes his first eastern tour to the old Manchu capital of Shengjing.
steps.text_zh: 1743年，首次东巡盛京，谒祖陵。

steps.text: 1746: Makes the first of several pilgrimages to the Buddhist mountain of Wutai.
steps.text_zh: 1746年，首次西巡五台山礼佛。

steps.text: 1748: Returning from Shandong, his beloved Empress Xiaoxian dies aboard their boat at Dezhou.
steps.text_zh: 1748年，东巡山东返京途中，孝贤皇后崩于德州舟中。

steps.text: 1751: Reaches Hangzhou on the first of six southern tours.
steps.text_zh: 1751年，首次南巡至杭州，此后共六下江南。

steps.text: 1773: Orders the compilation of the Complete Library of the Four Treasuries, combined with a purge of 'seditious' books.
steps.text_zh: 1773年，下令编纂《四库全书》，同时大规模禁毁书籍。

steps.text: 1780: Celebrates his seventieth birthday at Chengde with a visit from the Sixth Panchen Lama.
steps.text_zh: 1780年，七十寿辰，在承德接见六世班禅。

steps.text: 1784: Ends his sixth and last southern tour at Hangzhou.
steps.text_zh: 1784年，第六次也是最后一次南巡，至杭州。

steps.text: 1793: Receives Lord Macartney's British embassy at Chengde and rejects its trade requests.
steps.text_zh: 1793年，在承德接见英国马戛尔尼使团，拒绝其通商要求。

steps.text: 1799: Dies in the Forbidden City three years after abdicating; his favourite Heshen falls days later.
steps.text_zh: 1799年，禅位三年后崩于紫禁城，宠臣和珅随即倒台。

title: Zheng Banqiao's life
summary: One of the 'Eight Eccentrics of Yangzhou', Zheng Banqiao sold paintings in Yangzhou, passed the exams late, governed two Shandong counties with sympathy for the poor, and retired to paint bamboo.
summary_zh: 郑板桥是“扬州八怪”之一，早年在扬州卖画，中年中进士，在山东范县、潍县任知县体恤百姓，罢官后重回扬州卖画终老。

steps.text: 1693: Born in Xinghua into a poor scholar's family.
steps.text_zh: 1693年，生于江苏兴化一个清寒的读书人家。

steps.text: c. 1723: After his father's death he makes a living selling paintings in Yangzhou.
steps.text_zh: 约1723年，父亲去世后到扬州卖画为生。

steps.text: 1732: Passes the provincial examination in Nanjing at almost forty.
steps.text_zh: 1732年，年近四十，在南京考中举人。

steps.text: 1735: Studies in the monasteries of Jiaoshan island in the Yangtze while preparing for the metropolitan exams.
steps.text_zh: 1735年，寓居镇江焦山别峰庵读书备考。

steps.text: 1736: Becomes a jinshi in Beijing, but waits years for a post.
steps.text_zh: 1736年，在北京中进士，但长期候补。

steps.text: 1742: Appointed magistrate of Fan county in Shandong.
steps.text_zh: 1742年，出任山东范县知县。

steps.text: 1746: Transferred to Weixian, where he opens granaries during a famine without waiting for approval.
steps.text_zh: 1746年，调任潍县知县，遇大饥荒擅自开仓赈济。

steps.text: 1753: Resigns after offending his superiors and returns to sell paintings in Yangzhou.
steps.text_zh: 1753年，得罪上司辞官，回扬州卖画。

steps.text: 1766: Dies at home in Xinghua.
steps.text_zh: 1766年，卒于故乡兴化。

title: Cao Xueqin's life
summary: Born into a wealthy Nanjing family of imperial bondservants, Cao Xueqin saw it ruined and moved to Beijing, where he wrote Dream of the Red Chamber in poverty in the Western Hills.
summary_zh: 曹雪芹生于江宁织造的显赫之家，少年时家道败落，随家迁居北京，晚年隐居西山，在贫困中写成《红楼梦》。

steps.text: 1715: Born into the Cao family, hereditary Commissioners of the Imperial Silk Works at Jiangning (by most accounts).
steps.text_zh: 1715年，生于江宁织造曹家（一说），家族世代深得康熙宠信。

steps.text: 1728: After the Yongzheng Emperor confiscates the family's property, the household moves to a small house near Caishikou in Beijing.
steps.text_zh: 1728年，雍正抄没曹家，举家北迁，寄居北京崇文门外蒜市口老宅。

steps.place: Right Wing Imperial Clan School, Beijing
steps.text: c. 1750: Works at the Right Wing Imperial Clan School (by some accounts), where he befriends the Manchu poets Dunmin and Dunchéng.
steps.text_zh: 约1750年，一说在右翼宗学当差，与宗室诗人敦敏、敦诚兄弟结为好友。

steps.text: 1754: Living in poverty in the Western Hills, he keeps revising the novel; the 'Jiaxu' manuscript with Zhiyanzhai's comments dates from this year.
steps.text_zh: 1754年，已移居西山，“举家食粥”，仍反复增删小说，脂砚斋甲戌本即出于此年。

steps.text: c. 1759: By some accounts travels south to Nanjing, perhaps as a secretary on an official's staff, revisiting the city of his childhood.
steps.text_zh: 约1759年，一说南游江宁，入官员幕府，重访少年故地。

steps.text: 1760: Back in the Western Hills; his friends' poems describe him painting rocks and drinking to drown his sorrows.
steps.text_zh: 1760年，返回西山，敦敏等人诗中写他卖画沽酒、狂放不羁。

steps.text: 1763: Dies in the Western Hills on New Year's Eve (by one account), shortly after losing his young son, leaving the novel unfinished at 80 chapters.
steps.text_zh: 1763年除夕，幼子夭亡后不久病逝于西山（一说1764年），《红楼梦》仅存八十回。

title: Wu Jingzi's life
summary: A gentry heir from Quanjiao who squandered his fortune and turned his back on the exams, Wu Jingzi moved to Nanjing and wrote The Scholars, a satire of the examination world.
summary_zh: 吴敬梓出身全椒科第世家，散尽家财、厌弃科举，移居南京后写成讽刺科场百态的《儒林外史》。

steps.text: 1701: Born into a prominent scholar-official family in Quanjiao, Anhui.
steps.text_zh: 1701年，生于安徽全椒一个“科第仕宦多显者”的望族。

steps.text: 1714: Follows his adoptive father, appointed county director of schools, to Ganyu on the coast and studies there.
steps.text_zh: 1714年，随嗣父赴赣榆县教谕任，在任所读书。

steps.text: 1723: His father dies; family members quarrel over the inheritance and Wu begins to spend his share freely.
steps.text_zh: 1723年，嗣父去世，族人争夺遗产，吴敬梓从此挥霍家财。

steps.text: 1729: At the qualifying exam in Chuzhou he is criticised for his dissolute conduct and barely passes.
steps.text_zh: 1729年，赴滁州应科考，因“文章大好人大怪”遭考官训斥，勉强录取。

steps.text: 1733: Sells his old house and moves to a riverside pavilion on the Qinhuai in Nanjing, among poets and scholars.
steps.text_zh: 1733年，卖掉祖宅，移家南京，寓居秦淮水亭，与文士往来。

steps.text: 1736: Recommended for the special 'Erudite Scholars' examination, he sits the provincial round at Anqing but declines to go on to Beijing, pleading illness.
steps.text_zh: 1736年，被荐举博学鸿词科，赴安庆参加预试，后托病不赴京廷试，从此不再应举。

steps.text: c. 1750: Completes The Scholars in Nanjing, living in poverty and selling his books to buy food.
steps.text_zh: 约1750年，在南京贫困中写成《儒林外史》，常靠典卖书籍度日。

steps.text: 1754: Dies suddenly in Yangzhou while visiting friends there.
steps.text_zh: 1754年，客游扬州时猝然病逝。

title: Wei Yuan's life
summary: A Hunanese scholar who worked on statecraft and sea transport, Wei Yuan served on the coast during the Opium War and wrote the Illustrated Treatise on the Maritime Kingdoms urging China to learn from the West.
summary_zh: 魏源是湖南经世派学者，参与漕粮海运筹划，鸦片战争时投身浙东前线，编成《海国图志》，提出“师夷长技以制夷”。

steps.text: 1794: Born in Jintan, Shaoyang county, Hunan.
steps.text_zh: 1794年，生于湖南邵阳金潭。

steps.text: 1814: Comes to Beijing with his father and studies classical scholarship, including New Text studies under Liu Fenglu.
steps.text_zh: 1814年，随父入京，问学于刘逢禄等名家，研习今文经学。

steps.text: 1826: Helps plan the first shipment of tribute grain by sea from Shanghai to Tianjin, an alternative to the silted Grand Canal.
steps.text_zh: 1826年，参与筹划漕粮海运，首批漕粮由上海出海运往天津。

steps.text: 1831: Settles his family in Yangzhou, building the Jie Garden, his base for much of his later life.
steps.text_zh: 1831年，在扬州筑絜园定居，此后长期以扬州为家。

steps.text: 1841: Joins the staff of Commissioner Yuqian on the Zhejiang front of the Opium War and interrogates a captured British officer.
steps.text_zh: 1841年，入两江总督裕谦幕府，赴浙东镇海前线，曾亲审英军俘虏。

steps.text: 1842: Back in Yangzhou, compiles the Illustrated Treatise on the Maritime Kingdoms from Lin Zexu's translated materials.
steps.text_zh: 1842年，在扬州据林则徐所赠《四洲志》等资料编成《海国图志》。

steps.text: 1845: Finally passes the metropolitan examination at the age of 51.
steps.text_zh: 1845年，五十一岁始中进士。

steps.text: 1851: Serves as sub-prefect of Gaoyou; in 1853 he is dismissed amid the Taiping advance.
steps.text_zh: 1851年，任高邮知州，1853年太平军东进时被革职。

steps.text: 1857: Dies in a Buddhist monastery in Hangzhou, having turned to Buddhism in his last years.
steps.text_zh: 1857年，晚年潜心佛学，病逝于杭州僧舍。

title: Zeng Guofan's campaigns
summary: A Hunanese scholar-official who built the Xiang Army, Zeng Guofan led the long war against the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom and launched China's first modern arsenals.
summary_zh: 曾国藩以翰林出身创办湘军，历经十余年苦战平定太平天国，并开办安庆内军械所，开洋务运动之先。

steps.text: 1811: Born into a farming-gentry family at Baiyangping, Xiangxiang, Hunan.
steps.text_zh: 1811年，生于湖南湘乡白杨坪一个耕读之家。

steps.text: 1838: Passes the metropolitan exam and enters the Hanlin Academy, rising to vice-minister over the next decade.
steps.text_zh: 1838年，中进士，入翰林院，此后十年官至礼部侍郎。

steps.text: 1853: In mourning at home, he is ordered to raise militia, and trains the Xiang Army and its river fleet at Hengzhou.
steps.text_zh: 1853年，丁忧在籍，奉旨帮办团练，在衡州编练湘军陆师和水师。

steps.text: 1854: His first battle at Jinggang ends in a rout, and he tries to drown himself before being rescued.
steps.text_zh: 1854年，初战靖港大败，愤而投水，被部下救起。

steps.text: 1854: Having rallied, his army retakes Wuchang and Hanyang from the Taiping.
steps.text_zh: 1854年，重整旗鼓，湘军攻克武昌、汉阳。

steps.text: 1860: Appointed Viceroy of Liangjiang, he sets up headquarters at Qimen in the hills of southern Anhui.
steps.text_zh: 1860年，署理两江总督，移驻皖南祁门大营，几度身陷险境。

steps.text: 1861: His brother Zeng Guoquan takes Anqing; Zeng moves in and founds the Anqing Arsenal, the first of its kind.
steps.text_zh: 1861年，湘军攻克安庆，曾国藩移驻于此，创办安庆内军械所。

steps.text: 1864: The Xiang Army storms the Taiping capital Tianjing, ending the rebellion.
steps.text_zh: 1864年，湘军攻破天京，太平天国覆亡。

steps.text: 1870: As Viceroy of Zhili he handles the Tianjin Massacre, and his conciliatory settlement is widely denounced.
steps.text_zh: 1870年，以直隶总督查办天津教案，因妥协办案而饱受指责。

steps.text: 1872: Dies in office as Viceroy of Liangjiang at Nanjing.
steps.text_zh: 1872年，在两江总督任上病逝于南京。

title: Li Hongzhang's life
summary: Founder of the Huai Army and the leading statesman of late Qing self-strengthening, Li Hongzhang built arsenals and the Beiyang Fleet and signed the treaties that ended China's defeats.
summary_zh: 李鸿章创建淮军，主持洋务数十年，办军工、建北洋水师，又在屡次战败后代表清廷签订《马关条约》《辛丑条约》。

steps.text: 1823: Born at Modian near Hefei, Anhui, into a gentry family.
steps.text_zh: 1823年，生于安徽合肥磨店乡。

steps.text: 1847: Passes the metropolitan exam and studies under Zeng Guofan as a Hanlin scholar.
steps.text_zh: 1847年，中进士，入翰林院，师从曾国藩。

steps.text: 1853: Returns to Anhui to fight the Taiping with local militia.
steps.text_zh: 1853年，回乡办团练，在皖中与太平军作战。

steps.text: 1862: At Anqing, on Zeng Guofan's orders, he raises the Huai Army from Anhui militia.
steps.text_zh: 1862年，奉曾国藩之命，在安庆编成淮军。

steps.text: 1862: His troops are shipped down the Yangtze by British steamers to defend Shanghai; he becomes Governor of Jiangsu.
steps.text_zh: 1862年，淮军乘英国轮船东下上海，李鸿章署理江苏巡抚。

steps.text: 1863: Retakes Suzhou with Gordon's Ever-Victorious Army, then has the surrendered Taiping kings executed.
steps.text_zh: 1863年，会同戈登常胜军攻克苏州，杀降太平军诸王。

steps.text: 1865: Founds the Jiangnan Arsenal in Shanghai, China's largest modern factory.
steps.text_zh: 1865年，在上海创办江南制造总局。

steps.text: 1870: Becomes Viceroy of Zhili and Commissioner of the Northern Ports, based at Tianjin for 25 years.
steps.text_zh: 1870年，接任直隶总督兼北洋通商大臣，坐镇天津二十五年。

steps.text: 1895: Signs the Treaty of Shimonoseki after China's defeat; he is wounded by a Japanese assassin during the talks.
steps.text_zh: 1895年，赴日本马关议和，谈判期间遇刺受伤，签订《马关条约》。

steps.text: 1900: As Viceroy of Liangguang, he refuses the court's declaration of war on the powers during the Boxer crisis.
steps.text_zh: 1900年，任两广总督，义和团事起，拒不奉诏对列强宣战。

steps.text: 1901: Signs the Boxer Protocol in Beijing and dies two months later.
steps.text_zh: 1901年，在北京签订《辛丑条约》，两个月后病逝。

title: Zuo Zongtang's campaigns
summary: A Hunanese scholar who failed the top exams, Zuo Zongtang became a great general against the Taiping and Muslim rebels, built the Fuzhou shipyard and recovered Xinjiang.
summary_zh: 左宗棠三试不第，以幕僚起家，平定太平军和西北回乱，创办福州船政，抬棺出塞收复新疆。

steps.text: 1812: Born in Xiangyin, Hunan, to a family of poor scholars.
steps.text_zh: 1812年，生于湖南湘阴一个寒士之家。

steps.text: 1830: Studies at the Chengnan Academy in Changsha and meets the statecraft scholar He Changling; he passes the provincial exam in 1832 but fails in Beijing three times.
steps.text_zh: 1830年，就读长沙城南书院，结识经世派学者贺长龄，1832年中举，此后三次会试不第。

steps.text: 1840: Tutors the son of the late Viceroy Tao Shu at Anhua, reading his patron's library on geography and statecraft.
steps.text_zh: 1840年，在安化陶澍家坐馆授徒八年，遍读陶家藏书。

steps.text: 1852: Joins the staff of the Hunan governor and helps defend Changsha against the Taiping.
steps.text_zh: 1852年，入湖南巡抚张亮基幕府，协助守卫长沙抵御太平军。

steps.text: 1864: As Governor of Zhejiang, his Chu Army retakes Hangzhou from the Taiping.
steps.text_zh: 1864年，任浙江巡抚，率楚军收复杭州。

steps.text: 1866: As Viceroy of Min-Zhe, founds the Fuzhou Navy Yard at Mawei, China's first modern shipyard and naval school.
steps.text_zh: 1866年，任闽浙总督，在马尾创办福州船政局及船政学堂。

steps.text: 1872: After years of war against the Shaanxi–Gansu Muslim rebellion, he sets up headquarters in Lanzhou and builds an arsenal there.
steps.text_zh: 1872年，镇压陕甘回民起义后进驻兰州，开办兰州制造局。

steps.text: 1876: From his base at Suzhou in the Hexi Corridor he directs Liu Jintang's army into Xinjiang against Yakub Beg.
steps.text_zh: 1876年，坐镇肃州，指挥刘锦棠进军新疆，讨伐阿古柏。

steps.text: 1880: Marches to Hami with a coffin carried before him, to press Russia to return the Ili region.
steps.text_zh: 1880年，抬棺出关，进驻哈密，向沙俄施压索还伊犁。

steps.text: 1881: Called to Beijing to join the Grand Council.
steps.text_zh: 1881年，奉召入京，任军机大臣。

steps.text: 1885: Sent to oversee the defence of Fujian in the Sino-French War, he dies in Fuzhou.
steps.text_zh: 1885年，中法战争中督办福建军务，病逝于福州。

title: Hong Xiuquan's life
summary: A failed examination candidate from Guangdong who came to believe he was Christ's younger brother, Hong Xiuquan led the Taiping Rebellion and ruled from Nanjing until its fall.
summary_zh: 洪秀全屡试不第，自称上帝之子、耶稣之弟，发动太平天国起义，定都天京十一年，至城破前病逝。

steps.place_zh: 花县官禄㘵（今广州花都）
steps.text: 1814: Born into a Hakka farming family at Guanlubu, Hua County, near Guangzhou.
steps.text_zh: 1814年，生于广东花县官禄㘵一个客家农家。

steps.text: 1837: Fails the prefectural exam in Guangzhou for the third time, falls ill and has visions of heaven.
steps.text_zh: 1837年，第三次在广州应试落第，大病一场，梦见升天异象。

steps.text: 1844: After reading a Christian tract, he preaches with Feng Yunshan, travelling to Guixian in Guangxi.
steps.text_zh: 1844年，读《劝世良言》后创拜上帝会，与冯云山赴广西贵县传教。

steps.text: 1847: Studies the Bible for a few months with the American missionary Issachar Roberts.
steps.text_zh: 1847年，在广州随美国传教士罗孝全学习《圣经》数月。

steps.text: 1851: Proclaims the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom at the Jintian uprising.
steps.text_zh: 1851年，金田起义，建号太平天国。

steps.text: 1851: Takes Yong'an and enfeoffs his chief followers as the Eastern, Western, Southern and Northern Kings.
steps.text_zh: 1851年，攻占永安州，分封东、西、南、北、翼五王。

steps.text: 1853: The Taiping capture Wuchang, their first provincial capital, and sail down the Yangtze.
steps.text_zh: 1853年初，太平军攻克武昌，随即顺江东下。

steps.text: 1853: Takes Nanjing and makes it the Heavenly Capital; he rarely leaves his palace again.
steps.text_zh: 1853年，攻占南京，定都天京，此后深居天王府。

steps.text: 1864: Dies of illness in the besieged capital weeks before it falls to the Xiang Army.
steps.text_zh: 1864年，天京被围，病逝于天王府，一个多月后城破。

title: Liang Qichao's life
summary: A Cantonese prodigy and Kang Youwei's disciple, Liang Qichao led the 1898 reforms, spent fourteen years in exile in Japan as China's most influential journalist, and ended as a Tsinghua professor.
summary_zh: 梁启超少年中举，师从康有为，投身戊戌变法，流亡日本十四年间以报刊影响一代人，晚年执教清华。

steps.text: 1873: Born in Chakeng village, Xinhui, Guangdong.
steps.text_zh: 1873年，生于广东新会茶坑村。

steps.text: 1890: Already a provincial graduate at 16, he becomes a disciple of Kang Youwei at the Wanmu Caotang school.
steps.text_zh: 1890年，十六岁已中举，拜康有为为师，就读万木草堂。

steps.text: 1895: Helps Kang organise the 'Petition of the Examination Candidates' against the Treaty of Shimonoseki.
steps.text_zh: 1895年，随康有为发动公车上书，反对《马关条约》。

steps.text: 1896: Edits the reformist journal Shiwu Bao, making his name as a writer.
steps.text_zh: 1896年，在上海主笔《时务报》，声名鹊起。

steps.text: 1897: Becomes chief teacher at the Academy of Current Affairs in Changsha.
steps.text_zh: 1897年，赴长沙任时务学堂中文总教习。

steps.text: 1898: Takes part in the Hundred Days' Reform; when it is crushed he escapes on a Japanese warship.
steps.text_zh: 1898年，参与戊戌变法，政变后避入日本使馆，东渡日本。

steps.text: 1902: In exile, publishes the New Citizen Journal in Yokohama, read across China.
steps.text_zh: 1902年，流亡日本，在横滨创办《新民丛报》，风行国内。

steps.text: 1912: Returns to China after the revolution and later settles in Tianjin, where in 1915 he denounces Yuan Shikai's monarchy.
steps.text_zh: 1912年，民国成立后回国，后定居天津，1915年发表文章反对袁世凯称帝。

steps.text: 1925: Joins Tsinghua's Institute of Chinese Studies as one of its 'Four Great Tutors'.
steps.text_zh: 1925年，任清华国学研究院导师，与王国维等并称“四大导师”。

steps.text: 1929: Dies in Beijing after a botched kidney operation.
steps.text_zh: 1929年，病逝于北京协和医院。

title: Tan Sitong's life
summary: The son of a high official, Tan Sitong roamed China in his youth, became a radical reform thinker in Hunan, and chose to die in Beijing as one of the Six Gentlemen of 1898.
summary_zh: 谭嗣同出身官宦之家，少年游历南北，在湖南倡导新政，戊戌政变后拒绝出逃，成为“戊戌六君子”之一。

steps.text: 1865: Born in Beijing, where his father, from Liuyang in Hunan, is an official.
steps.text_zh: 1865年，生于北京宣武门外，父亲谭继洵为湖南浏阳人。

steps.text: 1877: Returns to his ancestral home of Liuyang to study after his mother's death.
steps.text_zh: 1877年，母亲去世后回原籍浏阳读书。

steps.text: c. 1884: Joins his father, now an official in Gansu, at Lanzhou, and travels widely in the northwest.
steps.text_zh: 约1884年，赴父亲任所甘肃兰州，游历西北各地。

steps.text: 1890: Lives at Wuchang after his father becomes Governor of Hubei.
steps.text_zh: 1890年，父亲升任湖北巡抚，随居武昌。

steps.text: 1895: Shaken by defeat in the war with Japan, he sets up a society for mathematics and science in Liuyang.
steps.text_zh: 1895年，甲午战败后发愤，在浏阳创办算学社。

steps.text: 1896: As an expectant prefect in Nanjing, he writes his radical treatise Renxue (On Benevolence).
steps.text_zh: 1896年，以候补知府身份在南京，写成《仁学》。

steps.text: 1897: Leads the Hunan reforms, helping found the Academy of Current Affairs and the Southern Study Society.
steps.text_zh: 1897年，回湖南推行新政，参与创办时务学堂、南学会。

steps.text: 1898: Called to Beijing as a secretary of the Grand Council during the Hundred Days' Reform.
steps.text_zh: 1898年，应召入京，以四品卿衔任军机章京，参与新政。

steps.text: 1898: Refuses to flee after the coup, saying reform needs blood, and is beheaded at Caishikou.
steps.text_zh: 1898年，政变后拒绝出逃，称“各国变法，无不从流血而成”，就义于菜市口。

title: Qiu Jin's life
summary: Qiu Jin left an arranged marriage to study in Japan, became a revolutionary and champion of women's rights, and was executed in Shaoxing after a failed uprising.
summary_zh: 秋瑾冲破包办婚姻东渡日本留学，投身革命、倡导女权，起义失败后在绍兴就义。

steps.text: 1875: Born in Xiamen, Fujian, where her grandfather was an official (by most accounts); her family is from Shaoxing.
steps.text_zh: 1875年，生于福建厦门（一说），祖籍浙江绍兴。

steps.text: 1896: Married into the wealthy Wang family of Xiangtan, Hunan.
steps.text_zh: 1896年，在湖南湘潭嫁入富商王家。

steps.text: 1903: Living in Beijing with her husband, she is radicalised by the Boxer aftermath and resolves to study abroad.
steps.text_zh: 1903年，随丈夫寓居北京，目睹国难，决意出洋求学。

steps.text: 1904: Leaves her family to study in Tokyo; in 1905 she joins the Revolutionary Alliance.
steps.text_zh: 1904年，变卖首饰东渡日本留学，1905年加入同盟会。

steps.text: 1906: Back in China, teaches at a girls' school in Nanxun.
steps.text_zh: 1906年，回国后在湖州南浔浔溪女校任教。

steps.text: 1907: Founds the China Women's Journal in Shanghai to argue for women's equality.
steps.text_zh: 1907年初，在上海创办《中国女报》，倡导男女平权。

steps.text: 1907: Heads the Datong School in Shaoxing to plan an uprising; she is arrested and beheaded at Xuanting Crossing.
steps.text_zh: 1907年，主持绍兴大通学堂，筹划起义，事泄被捕，就义于轩亭口。

title: Zhan Tianyou's life
summary: One of the first Chinese boys sent to study in America, Zhan Tianyou became China's pioneering railway engineer and built the Beijing–Zhangjiakou line without foreign help.
summary_zh: 詹天佑是首批留美幼童之一，学成归国后成为中国铁路工程的先驱，主持修建了中国人自主设计的京张铁路。

steps.text: 1861: Born in Guangzhou to a family of tea merchants from Wuyuan.
steps.text_zh: 1861年，生于广州西关，祖籍徽州婺源。

steps.text: 1872: Sails from Shanghai with the first group of the Chinese Educational Mission to the United States.
steps.text_zh: 1872年，作为首批留美幼童从上海启程赴美。

steps.text: 1882: After graduating in civil engineering from Yale in 1881, he is assigned to the Fuzhou naval school and fleet.
steps.text_zh: 1882年，耶鲁大学土木工程系毕业回国后，被派往福州船政学堂学习驾驶、在舰上服役。

steps.text: 1884: Teaches English at the Bowen Academy in Guangzhou and surveys the Guangdong coast.
steps.text_zh: 1884年，回广州任博学馆教习，并测绘广东沿海海图。

steps.text: 1888: Finally employed as a railway engineer on the Tianjin line of the China Railway Company.
steps.text_zh: 1888年，进入中国铁路公司任工程师，参与修建津沽铁路。

steps.text: 1892: Completes the Luanhe railway bridge after foreign engineers had failed.
steps.text_zh: 1892年，接手外国工程师失败的工程，建成滦河铁路大桥。

steps.text: 1905: As chief engineer of the Beijing–Zhangjiakou Railway, he takes the line over the Juyong Pass with a switchback at Qinglongqiao.
steps.text_zh: 1905年，任京张铁路总工程师，在青龙桥设“人”字形线路翻越八达岭。

steps.text: 1909: The line opens to Zhangjiakou, ahead of schedule and under budget.
steps.text_zh: 1909年，京张铁路全线通车，提前两年完工且节省经费。

steps.text: 1912: Heads the Guangdong company building the Canton–Hankow railway.
steps.text_zh: 1912年，在广州主持商办粤汉铁路。

steps.text: 1919: Dies in Hankou while supervising the Hankou–Guangdong–Sichuan railway system.
steps.text_zh: 1919年，督办汉粤川铁路期间病逝于汉口。

title: Yuan Shikai's life
summary: Rising from a military post in Korea to command the Qing's modern army, Yuan Shikai engineered the emperor's abdication, became president of the Republic and died after a failed bid to be emperor.
summary_zh: 袁世凯从驻朝鲜起家，编练新军掌握北洋，逼清帝退位而任民国大总统，最终因复辟帝制失败而死。

steps.text: 1859: Born at Zhangying in Xiangcheng, Henan, into a powerful official family.
steps.text_zh: 1859年，生于河南项城张营一个官宦大族。

steps.text: 1881: Having failed the exams, he joins the army of his father's friend Wu Changqing at Dengzhou.
steps.text_zh: 1881年，科场失意，投奔驻登州的淮军将领吴长庆。

steps.text: 1882: Goes to Korea with Wu's army to put down the Imo mutiny, and stays to dominate Korean affairs for twelve years, crushing the 1884 coup.
steps.text_zh: 1882年，随军入朝平定壬午兵变，此后留驻朝鲜十二年，1884年平定甲申政变。

steps.text: 1895: Trains the Newly Created Army at Xiaozhan near Tianjin, the core of the later Beiyang Army.
steps.text_zh: 1895年，在天津小站编练新建陆军，奠定北洋军基础。

steps.text: 1899: As Governor of Shandong he suppresses the Boxers in the province.
steps.text_zh: 1899年，任山东巡抚，严厉镇压义和团。

steps.text: 1902: As Viceroy of Zhili he recovers Tianjin from the allied powers and runs the New Policies from there.
steps.text_zh: 1902年，以直隶总督接收天津，大力推行新政，创建北洋六镇。

steps.text: 1909: Dismissed by the regent, he 'retires' to Huanshang village outside Zhangde, posing as a fisherman.
steps.text_zh: 1909年，被摄政王罢官，退居彰德洹上村，以“垂钓”示人。

steps.text: 1912: Recalled during the revolution, he forces the Qing emperor to abdicate and becomes president.
steps.text_zh: 1912年，辛亥革命中复出，逼清帝退位，就任中华民国临时大总统。

steps.text: 1916: His Hongxian monarchy collapses after 83 days; he dies in Beijing and is buried at Anyang.
steps.text_zh: 1916年，洪宪帝制八十三天而亡，袁世凯忧愤病逝于北京，归葬安阳。

title: Yan Fu's life
summary: Trained as a naval officer in Fuzhou and Britain, Yan Fu ran the Beiyang Naval Academy and became China's great translator of Western thought, introducing Darwin and Spencer through Evolution and Ethics.
summary_zh: 严复出身福州船政学堂，留学英国，主持北洋水师学堂多年，以《天演论》等译著把西方思想引入中国。

steps.text: 1854: Born in Houguan county, Fuzhou, the son of a doctor.
steps.text_zh: 1854年，生于福建侯官一个中医之家。

steps.text: 1867: Enters the new Fuzhou naval school after his father's death.
steps.text_zh: 1867年，父亲去世后考入福州船政学堂。

steps.text: 1877: Sent to the Royal Naval College at Greenwich, where he reads Western political and social thought.
steps.text_zh: 1877年，留学英国格林尼治皇家海军学院，广泛阅读西方社会政治学说。

steps.text: 1880: Becomes an instructor, and later head, of the Beiyang Naval Academy in Tianjin.
steps.text_zh: 1880年，任天津北洋水师学堂总教习，后升任总办。

steps.text: 1898: Publishes his translation Tianyan Lun (Huxley's Evolution and Ethics) after founding the Guowen Bao newspaper in Tianjin.
steps.text_zh: 1898年，在天津创办《国闻报》后，正式出版译著《天演论》。

steps.text: 1900: Flees the Boxer fighting to Shanghai, where he translates Mill and Adam Smith.
steps.text_zh: 1900年，避义和团之乱移居上海，翻译《原富》《群己权界论》等。

steps.text: 1906: Heads the Anhui Higher School in Anqing.
steps.text_zh: 1906年，任安徽高等学堂监督。

steps.text: 1912: Becomes the first president of Peking University; in 1915 he lends his name to Yuan Shikai's monarchist society.
steps.text_zh: 1912年，任北京大学首任校长；1915年列名筹安会。

steps.text: 1921: Dies in Fuzhou after returning home in ill health.
steps.text_zh: 1921年，病归福州，在家乡逝世。

title: Deng Shichang's life
summary: One of the first graduates of the Fuzhou naval school, Deng Shichang captained the cruiser Zhiyuan and died ramming toward a Japanese warship at the Battle of the Yellow Sea.
summary_zh: 邓世昌是福州船政学堂首批毕业生，任致远舰管带，在甲午黄海海战中开足马力冲向敌舰，与舰同沉。

steps.text: 1849: Born in Longdao village, Panyu, near Guangzhou, to a tea merchant's family.
steps.text_zh: 1849年，生于广东番禺龙导尾乡一个茶商家庭。

steps.text: c. 1860: Moves with his father to Shanghai and learns English from foreigners (by some accounts).
steps.text_zh: 约1860年，随父到上海，向外国人学习英语（一说）。

steps.text: 1867: Enters the first class of the Fuzhou naval school's navigation department.
steps.text_zh: 1867年，考入福州船政学堂驾驶班，为首届学生。

steps.text: 1874: Commands the gunboat Haidongyun guarding Penghu and Keelung during Japan's invasion of Taiwan.
steps.text_zh: 1874年，日本侵台期间，任“海东云”舰管带，巡守澎湖、基隆。

steps.text: 1880: Transferred by Li Hongzhang to the Beiyang navy at Tianjin.
steps.text_zh: 1880年，被李鸿章调入北洋水师。

steps.text: 1887: Goes to Britain to take delivery of the new cruiser Zhiyuan built at Elswick, and sails her home.
steps.text_zh: 1887年，赴英国接收在埃尔斯威克船厂建成的“致远”舰，率舰回国。

steps.text: 1888: Captain of the Zhiyuan as the Beiyang Fleet is formally established at Weihai.
steps.text_zh: 1888年，北洋水师正式成军，任“致远”舰管带。

steps.text: 1894: At the Battle of the Yellow Sea, his damaged ship charges the Japanese cruiser Yoshino and sinks; he refuses rescue and drowns with his crew.
steps.text_zh: 1894年，黄海海战中，致远舰重伤后冲向日舰吉野，被击沉，邓世昌拒绝救援，与舰同沉。

title: Wang Fuzhi's life
summary: A Ming loyalist from Hengyang who fought the Qing conquest and briefly served the Yongli court, Wang Fuzhi spent forty years in hiding in the Hunan hills writing philosophy and history.
summary_zh: 王夫之是衡阳人，明亡后起兵抗清、投奔永历朝廷，失败后隐居湘西石船山四十年，著书立说。

steps.text: 1619: Born in Hengyang, Hunan, the son of a scholar.
steps.text_zh: 1619年，生于湖南衡阳一个书香之家。

steps.text: 1642: Passes the provincial examination at Wuchang.
steps.text_zh: 1642年，赴武昌乡试中举。

steps.text: 1648: Raises a loyalist force at Mount Heng against the Qing, which is quickly defeated.
steps.text_zh: 1648年，在南岳衡山举兵抗清，兵败。

steps.text: 1650: Joins the Southern Ming Yongli court at Zhaoqing as a minor official, but is caught up in factional strife.
steps.text_zh: 1650年，投奔肇庆永历朝廷，任行人司行人，卷入党争几遭不测。

steps.text: 1650: Takes refuge with the loyalist commander Qu Shisi at Guilin, leaving just before the city falls.
steps.text_zh: 1650年，往桂林依瞿式耜，城破前离去。

steps.text: 1653: Hides in the mountains of Changning, dressed as a Yao tribesman, and teaches local students.
steps.text_zh: 1653年，避居常宁山中，变姓名、着瑶服，为当地学子讲学。

steps.text: 1675: Builds the Xiangxi Caotang hut below Stone Boat Mountain, where he writes most of his works.
steps.text_zh: 1675年，在石船山下筑湘西草堂，此后在此潜心著述。

steps.text: 1692: Dies at his hut, having never shaved his head in the Manchu style.
steps.text_zh: 1692年，终老湘西草堂，至死未曾剃发。

title: Pu Songling's life
summary: A brilliant youth who failed the provincial exam for half a century, Pu Songling spent most of his life as a private tutor in Shandong and wrote the ghost tales of Strange Stories from a Chinese Studio.
summary_zh: 蒲松龄少年成名，此后乡试屡试不第，大半生在淄川乡间坐馆教书，写成《聊斋志异》。

steps.text: 1640: Born in Pujia village, Zichuan, Shandong, to a merchant family.
steps.text_zh: 1640年，生于山东淄川蒲家庄。

steps.text: 1658: Takes first place in the county, prefectural and provincial qualifying exams, praised by the examiner Shi Runzhang.
steps.text_zh: 1658年，县、府、道试皆第一，受学道施闰章赏识。

steps.text: 1670: Goes south to serve as secretary to his friend Sun Hui, magistrate of Baoying in Jiangsu.
steps.text_zh: 1670年，南下江苏宝应，为知县孙蕙作幕宾。

steps.text: 1671: Accompanies Sun to Gaoyou, then returns home disappointed later that year.
steps.text_zh: 1671年，随孙蕙赴高邮，当年秋辞幕北归。

steps.text: 1672: Tours Mount Lao with friends; the mountain later appears in his tale of the Daoist of Laoshan.
steps.text_zh: 1672年，与友人同游崂山，后写成《崂山道士》。

steps.text: 1679: Begins some thirty years as tutor in the Bi family at Xipu, and writes the preface to his Liaozhai tales.
steps.text_zh: 1679年，到西铺毕家坐馆，前后三十年，同年为《聊斋志异》作序。

steps.text: 1687: Disqualified again at the provincial exam in Jinan for a slip in his paper.
steps.text_zh: 1687年，在济南乡试因“越幅”被黜。

steps.text: 1711: Goes to Qingzhou at 71 to be made a senior licentiate (by some accounts).
steps.text_zh: 1711年，七十一岁赴青州考取岁贡生（一说）。

steps.text: 1715: Dies at home in Pujia village.
steps.text_zh: 1715年，病逝于蒲家庄。

title: Zhang Zhidong's life
summary: A scholar-official who governed from Sichuan to Guangdong, Zhang Zhidong built Wuhan into an industrial centre and promoted 'Chinese learning as the base, Western learning for use'.
summary_zh: 张之洞历任多省督抚，在湖北兴办汉阳铁厂、枪炮厂和新式学堂，提出“中学为体，西学为用”。

steps.text: 1837: Born in Xingyi, Guizhou, where his father is prefect; his family is from Nanpi in Zhili.
steps.text_zh: 1837年，生于父亲任所贵州兴义，祖籍直隶南皮。

steps.text: 1863: Places third (tanhua) in the palace examination.
steps.text_zh: 1863年，殿试一甲第三名，中探花。

steps.text: 1867: Serves as Hubei education commissioner and founds an academy at Wuchang.
steps.text_zh: 1867年，任湖北学政，创办经心书院。

steps.text: 1874: As Sichuan education commissioner, founds the Zunjing Academy in Chengdu.
steps.text_zh: 1874年，任四川学政，在成都创办尊经书院。

steps.text: 1881: As Governor of Shanxi he tackles famine relief and opium.
steps.text_zh: 1881年，任山西巡抚，整顿吏治、禁种罂粟。

steps.text: 1884: As Viceroy of Liangguang he directs Guangdong's role in the Sino-French War.
steps.text_zh: 1884年，任两广总督，筹划中法战争，起用冯子材。

steps.text: 1890: Now Viceroy of Huguang, he founds the Hanyang Iron Works and arsenal.
steps.text_zh: 1890年，调任湖广总督，创办汉阳铁厂、湖北枪炮厂。

steps.text: 1894: Acting Viceroy of Liangjiang during the war with Japan, he founds the Self-Strengthening Army.
steps.text_zh: 1894年，署理两江总督，编练自强军。

steps.text: 1898: Back in Wuchang, he publishes Exhortation to Study, setting out 'Chinese learning as the base'.
steps.text_zh: 1898年，回任湖广总督，撰《劝学篇》，提出“中体西用”。

steps.text: 1909: Having joined the Grand Council in 1907, he dies in Beijing.
steps.text_zh: 1909年，1907年入军机处后，病逝于北京。

title: Ji Yun's life
summary: A witty Hanlin scholar from Zhili, Ji Yun survived exile in Urumqi to become chief editor of the Siku Quanshu and wrote the tales of Notes from the Hut for Close Scrutiny.
summary_zh: 纪昀以才学入翰林，曾谪戍乌鲁木齐，归来后任《四库全书》总纂官，晚年写成《阅微草堂笔记》。

steps.text: 1724: Born at Cui'erzhuang in Xian County, Zhili.
steps.text_zh: 1724年，生于直隶献县崔尔庄。

steps.text: 1754: Passes the metropolitan exam and enters the Hanlin Academy.
steps.text_zh: 1754年，中进士，入翰林院。

steps.text: 1763: Serves as education commissioner of Fujian.
steps.text_zh: 1763年，出任福建学政。

steps.text: 1769: Exiled to Urumqi for warning a relative of an impending investigation; he records frontier life in verse.
steps.text_zh: 1769年，因向亲家卢见曾泄密获罪，谪戍乌鲁木齐，写下《乌鲁木齐杂诗》。

steps.text: 1773: Recalled and made chief editor of the Siku Quanshu, the vast imperial library.
steps.text_zh: 1773年，召还入京，任《四库全书》总纂官。

steps.text: 1787: Goes to the Chengde summer palace to check the Wenjin Pavilion copy of the Siku Quanshu.
steps.text_zh: 1787年，赴承德避暑山庄校勘文津阁《四库全书》。

steps.text: 1789: Begins Notes from the Hut for Close Scrutiny at his home near Hufangqiao.
steps.text_zh: 1789年，在虎坊桥阅微草堂开始撰写《阅微草堂笔记》。

steps.text: 1805: Dies in Beijing as Assistant Grand Secretary.
steps.text_zh: 1805年，以协办大学士卒于北京。

title: Shitao's travels
summary: A Ming prince orphaned at the fall of the dynasty, Shitao became a wandering Buddhist monk-painter, met the Kangxi Emperor twice, and ended his days as a professional painter in Yangzhou.
summary_zh: 石涛本是明宗室，幼年家破，出家为僧，云游各地作画，曾两度接驾康熙，晚年定居扬州卖画。

steps.text: 1642: Born Zhu Ruoji, a descendant of the Ming prince of Jingjiang, in Guilin.
steps.text_zh: 1642年，生于桂林靖江王府，本名朱若极。

steps.text: 1645: After his father is killed in a power struggle, a servant takes him to safety at the Xiangshan Temple in Quanzhou.
steps.text_zh: 1645年，父亲在内斗中被杀，由家仆携至全州湘山寺避难。

steps.text: c. 1662: Studies Chan Buddhism under the monk Lü'an Benyue in Songjiang.
steps.text_zh: 约1662年，在松江拜旅庵本月为师，研习禅学。

steps.text: 1666: Settles at Xuancheng for some fifteen years, painting Mount Huang and Jingting Mountain.
steps.text_zh: 1666年，寓居宣城敬亭山一带约十五年，多次登黄山写生。

steps.text: 1684: Living at the Changgan Temple in Nanjing since 1680, he greets the Kangxi Emperor on his first southern tour.
steps.text_zh: 1684年，自1680年起居南京长干寺一枝阁，康熙南巡时接驾。

steps.text: 1689: Meets the Kangxi Emperor again at Yangzhou.
steps.text_zh: 1689年，在扬州再次接驾康熙。

steps.text: 1690: Travels to Beijing seeking patronage and paints for court officials.
steps.text_zh: 1690年，北上京师，结交权贵，为王公作画。

steps.text: 1697: Settles for good in Yangzhou, builds the Dadi Hall and lives as a Daoist-leaning professional painter.
steps.text_zh: 1697年，定居扬州，建大涤草堂，以卖画为生。

steps.text: 1707: Dies in Yangzhou.
steps.text_zh: 1707年，卒于扬州。

title: Liu Mingchuan's life
summary: A Huai Army general from Hefei, Liu Mingchuan fought the Taiping and Nian, defended Taiwan against France, and as its first governor built its first railway.
summary_zh: 刘铭传是合肥人，淮军名将，转战平定太平军和捻军，中法战争中保卫台湾，任台湾首任巡抚并修建台湾第一条铁路。

steps.text: 1836: Born into a poor farming family below Daqian Mountain, Hefei.
steps.text_zh: 1836年，生于合肥大潜山下一个贫苦农家。

steps.text: 1862: Joins Li Hongzhang's Huai Army and goes to Shanghai at the head of the 'Ming' battalions.
steps.text_zh: 1862年，率铭字营加入淮军，随李鸿章赴上海。

steps.text: 1864: Helps capture Changzhou from the Taiping.
steps.text_zh: 1864年，参与攻克常州。

steps.text: 1867: Defeats the Eastern Nian army in Shandong, crushing it near Shouguang.
steps.text_zh: 1867年，在山东寿光一带大败东捻军。

steps.text: 1868: Retires home on grounds of illness and lives quietly for many years.
steps.text_zh: 1868年，称病回乡，隐居大潜山房多年。

steps.text: 1884: Sent to Taiwan in the Sino-French War, he defends Keelung against the French.
steps.text_zh: 1884年，中法战争中督办台湾军务，坚守基隆。

steps.text: 1884: Repels the French landing at Tamsui.
steps.text_zh: 1884年，在沪尾击退法军登陆。

steps.text: 1887: As first Governor of Taiwan Province, he builds the Keelung–Taipei railway, telegraphs and a modern post.
steps.text_zh: 1887年，任台湾首任巡抚，修建基隆至台北铁路，开设电报、邮政。

steps.text: 1896: Dies at home, reportedly grief-stricken by Taiwan's cession to Japan.
steps.text_zh: 1896年，闻台湾割让日本，忧愤成疾，病逝于家乡。
